notes.NC26.4.SGMR.1: Protractor reading cannot be tested fairly without a figure, so the questions test degrees as parts of a circle, estimating and classifying angles, and finding unknown angles by adding and subtracting.
notes.NC26.4.RD.1: Line plots, bar graphs and double bar graphs are always described in words or numbers, never drawn. Medians are of an odd number of values, or of an even number whose two middle values are equal. Four questions use half or quarter inches on a line plot (like-denominator subtraction only).
notes.NC26.4.ANR.7: Shape patterns are described by their counts (toothpicks in each figure).
notes.NC26.4.SGMR.2: Text only: no figures. Triangles are classified by angles (acute, right, obtuse) and by sides (scalene, isosceles, equilateral); isosceles is never offered next to an equilateral triangle, and trapezoid is used only when the stem says exactly one pair of parallel sides, so definitions that differ between textbooks cannot make a second option defensible. Notation uses \overline, \overrightarrow and \overleftrightarrow.
notes.NC26.4.ANR.3: All numbers stay within grade 4: prime and composite within 100, factors of numbers to 100, products up to four digits by one digit and two digits by two digits, quotients up to four digits by one digit. Every question is text only. Eight skills named in the summary, 8 to 14 questions each.
notes.NC26.4.ANR.4: Three families named in the summary: problems with all four operations (36 questions in seven kinds), equations with a letter for the unknown (28), and checking answers by estimation (26). Numbers stay within grade 4 whole numbers. Every question is text only. Some stretch (difficulty 3) problems have three operations or a reverse step, always with whole numbers and no fractions or decimals.
notes.NC26.4.ANR.5: Text only. Models are described in words; the answers are fractions with denominators 2 to 12 and 100, decimals to hundredths. Fractions like 3/4 and 1/4 are used as decimals only through hundredths.
notes.NC26.4.ANR.6: Text only. Denominators are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12; every sum and difference has a like denominator. Answers may be given as a fraction or a mixed number (any equivalent form is accepted by the checker).
notes.NC26.4.SGMR.3: Text only. Times are written out with a.m./p.m.; a time answer is a choice, and a numeric answer asks how many minutes after a given hour (for example, how many minutes after 4:00 p.m. an event ends). Conversions all go from a larger unit to a smaller one (and one division of centimeters into pieces); no answer is a decimal. Estimate questions use common benchmarks (a pencil about 19 cm, a loaf of bread about 500 g, a cup about 250 mL).
notes.NC26.4.SGMR.4: Whole-number sides throughout; no division by a two-digit number. Rectilinear figures are described by their parts or by the lengths of their sides, never a picture. Fixed-area questions list whole-number factor pairs only.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 7 in $47{,}215$?
questions.solution: The 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is $7 \times 1{,}000 = 7{,}000$.

questions.skill: Word form to standard form
questions.stem: Which number is forty-two thousand, six hundred five?
questions.solution: Forty-two thousand is $42{,}000$; six hundred five is $605$. Together: $42{,}605$.

questions.skill: Expanded form to standard form
questions.solution: 3 ten thousands, 6 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones make $36{,}409$.

questions.skill: Comparing numbers
questions.stem: Which comparison is true?
questions.solution: Both start with $56$ thousands. In the hundreds place, $0 < 1$, so $56{,}091 < 56{,}109$.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: In $33{,}333$, the value of the digit in the thousands place is how many times the value of the digit in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: The thousands digit is worth $3{,}000$ and the hundreds digit $300$. $3{,}000 \div 300 = 10$.

questions.skill: Ordering numbers
questions.stem: Which list puts $70{,}512$, $70{,}215$ and $75{,}021$ in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: $75{,}021$ has the most thousands, so it is greatest. Of the other two, $70{,}215$ has fewer hundreds than $70{,}512$.

questions.skill: Adding without regrouping
Subtracting thousands
questions.solution: $9$ thousands take away $3$ thousands leaves $6$ thousands: $6{,}000$.

questions.skill: Adding with regrouping
questions.solution: With the standard algorithm, regrouping the ones, tens and thousands: $38{,}406 + 17{,}859 = 56{,}265$.

questions.skill: Subtracting across zeros
Two steps: subtract, then add
questions.stem: A library had $52{,}318$ books. It gave away $8{,}749$ books and then bought $3{,}560$ new ones. How many books does it have now?

questions.skill: Missing addend
questions.stem: What number goes in the box? $\square + 27{,}085 = 63{,}000$

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a 5-digit number
questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 7 in the number $37{,}428$?
questions.solution: Read the places from the left: 3 is in the ten-thousands place, 7 is in the thousands place, 4 is in the hundreds place, 2 is in the tens place and 8 is in the ones place. So the 7 stands for 7 thousands, which is 7,000.

solve.work: In 37,428 the 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7 x 1,000 = 7,000.

questions.skill: Standard form from expanded form
questions.stem: Write the number as digits: $60{,}000 + 4{,}000 + 300 + 5$.
questions.solution: There are 6 ten-thousands, 4 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones. The number is 64,305.

questions.skill: Compare 5-digit numbers
questions.stem: Which of these numbers is the greatest?
questions.solution: Compare from the left. All four have 4 ten-thousands, and 40,968 has only 0 thousands, so it is the least. The other three have 1 thousand. Compare the hundreds: 41,086 has 0, while 41,680 and 41,608 each have 6. Compare the tens: 41,680 has 8 and 41,608 has 0. So 41,680 is the greatest.

solve.work: All have 4 ten-thousands. 40,968 has 0 thousands, the rest 1, so it is not greatest. Among 41,608, 41,680, 41,086 compare hundreds: 6, 6, 0; then tens: 41,608 has 0 tens, 41,680 has 8 tens. Greatest is 41,680.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: Look at the number $83{,}519$. What is the value of the digit 3?
questions.solution: The 3 is in the thousands place (8 ten-thousands, 3 thousands, ...), so its value is 3 thousands, or 3,000.

solve.work: 83,519: digits 8 (ten-thousands), 3 (thousands), 5, 1, 9. The 3 is in the thousands place, so its value is 3 x 1,000 = 3,000.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: In $58{,}326$, what is the value of the digit 8?
questions.solution: The 8 is in the thousands place, so its value is 8 thousands = 8,000.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 9 in $91{,}704$?
questions.solution: The 9 is in the ten-thousands place, so its value is 9 ten-thousands = 90,000.

solve.work: 91,704: 9 is in the ten-thousands place, value 90,000.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: What digit is in the ten-thousands place of $61{,}438$?
questions.solution: The first digit of a five-digit number is in the ten-thousands place. In 61,438 it is 6.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: In $45{,}982$, which place is the digit 5 in?
questions.solution: The places, from the left, are ten-thousands (4), thousands (5), hundreds (9), tens (8) and ones (2). The 5 is in the thousands place.

solve.work: 45,982: 4 ten-thousands, 5 thousands. The 5 is in the thousands place.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: Which digit is in the tens place of $83{,}640$?
questions.solution: The places, from the right, are ones (0), tens (4), hundreds (6), thousands (3), ten-thousands (8). The tens digit is 4.

solve.work: 83,640: 8 ten-thousands, 3 thousands, 6 hundreds, 4 tens, 0 ones. Tens digit 4.

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.stem: A number has 7 ten-thousands, 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 1 ten and 6 ones. Which number is it?
questions.solution: Write each count in its place: 7 ten-thousands, 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 1 ten, 6 ones makes 72,416.

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.stem: Which number is the same as $50{,}000 + 700 + 30 + 2$?
questions.solution: 50,000 + 700 + 30 + 2: there are 5 ten-thousands, 0 thousands, 7 hundreds, 3 tens and 2 ones, which is 50,732.

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.solution: 10,000 + 8,000 = 18,000; then add 700 and 6 to get 18,706 (there are no tens).

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: $62{,}508 = 60{,}000 + 2{,}000 + \square + 8$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: The digit 5 in 62,508 is in the hundreds place, so the missing part is 500.

solve.work: 62,508: 6 ten-thousands, 2 thousands, 5 hundreds, 0 tens, 8 ones. Missing part is 500.

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: Which shows $36{,}420$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: 3 ten-thousands = 30,000; 6 thousands = 6,000; 4 hundreds = 400; 2 tens = 20; 0 ones. So 36,420 = 30,000 + 6,000 + 400 + 20.

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the parts when $53{,}164$ is written in expanded form?
questions.solution: 53,164 = 50,000 + 3,000 + 100 + 60 + 4. The part 600 is not in the list, because the 6 is in the tens place (60).

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: Which is the word name for $35{,}200$?
questions.solution: 35,200 is 35 thousand and 200: thirty-five thousand, two hundred.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: Write eighty-three thousand, four hundred fifty-one using digits.
questions.solution: 83 thousand is 83,000; four hundred fifty-one is 451. Together: 83,451.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: How is $90{,}007$ read aloud?
questions.solution: 90,007 is 90 thousand and 7: ninety thousand, seven.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: How many times as much is $7{,}000$ as $700$?
questions.solution: 7,000 is 7 thousands and 700 is 7 hundreds. A thousand is 10 times a hundred, so 7,000 is 10 times as much as 700.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: In our number system, each place has a value how many times the value of the place to its right?
questions.solution: 10 ones make a ten, 10 tens make a hundred, and so on: each place is 10 times the place to its right.

solve.work: Base ten: each place is 10 times the place to its right.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: Which number is 10 times as much as $6{,}000$?
questions.solution: 10 times 6,000 is 60,000: 6 thousands become 6 ten-thousands.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: Four trucks hauled $38{,}620$, $38{,}260$, $36{,}820$ and $36{,}280$ pounds of gravel. Which amount is the least?
questions.solution: Compare from the left: all four start with 3. The thousands digits are 8, 8, 6, 6, so the two with 6 thousands are least. Then 280 < 820, so 36,280 is the least.

solve.work: 36,xxx < 38,xxx. Between 36,820 and 36,280: hundreds 2 < 8, so 36,280 is least.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: Which is greater, $29{,}845$ or $29{,}854$? Type the greater number.
questions.solution: The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 29,854 is greater.

solve.work: 29,845 vs 29,854: same through hundreds (8); tens 4 < 5, so 29,854 is greater.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: Which number is greater than $67{,}400$?
questions.solution: 67,410 is 10 more than 67,400, so it is greater. The other three are all less than 67,400.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Which list shows the numbers in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: 8,500 has only 4 digits, so it is least. Then 24,000 < 41,000. The order is 8,500; 24,000; 41,000.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Three numbers are $35{,}000$, $53{,}000$ and $5{,}300$. If they are put in order from least to greatest, which number is in the middle?
questions.solution: Order: 5,300 < 35,000 < 53,000. The middle number is 35,000.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Three towns have $91{,}200$, $19{,}200$ and $9{,}120$ people. Which list puts the towns' populations from greatest to least?
questions.solution: 91,200 is greatest, then 19,200, then 9,120 (only four digits).

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: How many hundreds are in $3{,}000$?
questions.solution: 10 hundreds make 1 thousand, so 3 thousands is 30 hundreds.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: Which is equal to 5 thousands?
questions.solution: 1 thousand = 10 hundreds, so 5 thousands = 50 hundreds.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: A toy store packs balls in bags of 10. How many bags can be filled with 700 balls?
questions.solution: There are 70 tens in 700, so 70 bags can be filled.

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: A five-digit number has a 7 in the ten-thousands place, a 7 in the ones place, and 0 in every other place. What is the number?
questions.solution: Put 7 in the ten-thousands place, 0 in thousands, hundreds and tens, and 7 in the ones place: 70,007.

solve.work: 7 in ten-thousands, 0 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 7 ones: 70,007.

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: Use the digits 4, 9, 2, 6 and 1 once each to make the greatest five-digit number you can.
questions.solution: Put the digits in order from greatest to least: 9, 6, 4, 2, 1. The number is 96,421.

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: Which number has a 6 in the ten-thousands place?
questions.solution: The ten-thousands digit is the first digit of a five-digit number. 64,201 starts with 6.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: In the number $26{,}640$, the first 6 (in the thousands place) is worth how many times as much as the second 6 (in the hundreds place)?
questions.solution: The first 6 is worth 6,000 and the second 6 is worth 600. Since $6{,}000 \div 600 = 10$, the first 6 is worth 10 times as much. Each place is 10 times the place to its right.

solve.work: Thousands 6 is worth 6,000; hundreds 6 is worth 600. 6,000 / 600 = 10.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a 5-digit number with zeros
questions.stem: Which shows $50{,}209$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: The 5 is in the ten-thousands place, so it is worth 50,000. The thousands digit is 0. The 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 200. The tens digit is 0, and the 9 is 9 ones. So $50{,}209 = 50{,}000 + 200 + 9$.

questions.skill: Order three 5-digit numbers
questions.stem: Which list puts $35{,}412$, $34{,}999$ and $35{,}142$ in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: 34,999 has 4 thousands, so it is the least. The other two both have 5 thousands, so compare the hundreds: 35,142 has 1 hundred and 35,412 has 4 hundreds. From least to greatest: 34,999; 35,142; 35,412.

solve.work: 34,999 < 35,142 < 35,412 (34 thousand is least; then 35,142 has 1 hundred vs 4 hundreds).

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: In $52{,}830$, which digit has a value of $2{,}000$?
questions.solution: Value 2,000 means 2 thousands. The digit in the thousands place of 52,830 is 2.

solve.work: 52,830: 5 ten-thousands (50,000), 2 thousands (2,000), 8 hundreds, 3 tens, 0 ones. The digit worth 2,000 is 2.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: In $13{,}340$, the digit 3 appears twice. Reading from the left, which statement is true?
choices: The first 3 is worth 300 and the second 3 is worth 30.
The first 3 is worth 3,000 and the second 3 is worth 300.
The first 3 is worth 30,000 and the second 3 is worth 3,000.
questions.answer: The first 3 is worth 3,000 and the second 3 is worth 300.
questions.solution: In 13,340 the first 3 is in the thousands place (3,000) and the second 3 is in the hundreds place (300).

solve.answer: The first 3 is worth 3,000 and the second 3 is worth 300.
solve.work: 13,340: 1 ten-thousand, 3 thousands, 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 0 ones. First 3 = 3,000, second 3 = 300.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: A stadium sold $48{,}250$ tickets. In that number, the digit 5 stands for how many tickets?
questions.solution: The 5 is in the tens place, so it stands for 5 tens = 50 tickets.

solve.work: 48,250: 4 ten-thousands, 8 thousands, 2 hundreds, 5 tens, 0 ones. The 5 is in the tens place, value 50.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: Look at the number $52{,}738$. What do you get when you add the digit in the thousands place to the digit in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: The thousands digit is 2 and the hundreds digit is 7. Then 2 + 7 = 9.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: Which number has the digit 7 in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: In 41,723 the digits are 4 ten-thousands, 1 thousand, 7 hundreds, 2 tens, 3 ones. The other numbers have the 7 in the thousands, tens and ones places.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: In $34{,}941$, the digit 4 appears twice. In which place is the second 4 (reading from the left)?
questions.solution: The digits are 3 (ten-thousands), 4 (thousands), 9 (hundreds), 4 (tens), 1 (ones). The second 4 is in the tens place.

solve.work: 34,941: 3 ten-thousands, 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 4 tens, 1 one. Second 4 is in the tens place.

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.stem: Write $8{,}000 + 60{,}000 + 9$ as a number.
questions.solution: The parts are in a mixed-up order. 60,000 + 8,000 + 9 = 68,009 (0 hundreds and 0 tens).

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.stem: Mia wrote a number that has 3 ten-thousands, 8 hundreds and 4 ones. Which number did she write?
questions.solution: 3 ten-thousands is 30,000; there are 0 thousands, 8 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones, so the number is 30,804.

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.stem: A number is 6 thousands, 5 tens and 2 ones more than $40{,}000$. What is the number?

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: A number is written in expanded form by adding the value of each digit that is not zero. How many numbers are added to write $90{,}206$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: 90,206 = 90,000 + 200 + 6. The digits that are not zero are 9, 2 and 6, so 3 numbers are added.

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: Which shows $91{,}240$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: Read each digit with its place: 9 ten-thousands, 1 thousand, 2 hundreds, 4 tens, and 0 ones.

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: $42{,}815 = 40{,}000 + 2{,}000 + 800 + \square + 5$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: The digit 1 in 42,815 is in the tens place, so it is worth 10.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: A car's odometer reads seventy thousand, nine hundred three miles. Type the number of miles in digits.
questions.solution: 70 thousand is 70,000, and 903 follows it, so the number is 70,903.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: Which is the word form of $48{,}050$?
questions.solution: 48,050 is 48 thousand and 50: forty-eight thousand, fifty.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: Mr. Lee reads aloud "fifty-six thousand, seventy-one." In that number, what digit is in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: Fifty-six thousand, seventy-one is 56,071. The digits are 5, 6, 0, 7, 1, so the hundreds digit is 0.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: A school library has $3{,}200$ books. A larger library has 10 times as many books. How many books does the larger library have?
questions.solution: 10 x 3,200 = 32,000. Each digit moves one place to the left.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: $28{,}000$ is 10 times as much as what number?
questions.solution: Divide by 10: 28,000 / 10 = 2,800. Each digit moves one place to the right.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: Which statement about the digit 5 in $55{,}120$ is true?
choices: The first 5 is worth 100 times as much as the second 5.
The two 5s are worth the same amount.
The first 5 is worth 10 times as much as the second 5.
The second 5 is worth 10 times as much as the first 5.
questions.answer: The first 5 is worth 10 times as much as the second 5.
questions.solution: The first 5 is in the ten-thousands place (50,000) and the second is in the thousands place (5,000). 50,000 is 10 times 5,000.

solve.answer: The first 5 is worth 10 times as much as the second 5.
solve.work: 55,120: first 5 = 50,000, second 5 = 5,000. 50,000 = 10 x 5,000, so the first is 10 times the second.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: The first three digits decide: 72,4 vs 72,0 means 72,406 is greater than 72,046. It is less than 72,640 and not equal to 72,460.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: Of $62{,}045$, $62{,}405$ and $62{,}054$, which number is the least?
questions.solution: All three start with 62. Next compare the hundreds: 0, 4, 0. The two with 0 hundreds are less; of those, 45 < 54. So 62,045 is the least.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: Three schools collected $31{,}408$, $31{,}480$ and $30{,}948$ cans for a food drive. How many cans did the school that collected the most collect?
questions.solution: 30,948 is least because it has 0 thousands. Compare 31,408 and 31,480: the tens digit 8 > 0, so 31,480 is the most.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: The numbers $12{,}450$; $12{,}045$; $12{,}504$ and $12{,}540$ are put in order from least to greatest. Which number is third?

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Four parks had these numbers of visitors in one year: $40{,}615$; $46{,}015$; $40{,}651$; $46{,}105$. Which list shows the visitor counts from least to greatest?
questions.solution: Compare thousands first: 40 < 46. Among 40,615 and 40,651: 615 < 651. Among 46,015 and 46,105: 015 < 105.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Cards show $27{,}630$; $27{,}360$; $26{,}730$ and $27{,}306$. The cards are put in order from greatest to least. Which number is second?
questions.solution: Greatest to least: 27,630; 27,360; 27,306; 26,730. The second number is 27,360.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: Write 36 hundreds and 5 ones as a number.
questions.solution: 36 hundreds is 3,600. Adding 5 ones gives 3,605.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: Which is another way to write $52{,}000$?
questions.solution: 52,000 is 52 thousands. 52 hundreds is only 5,200.

solve.work: 52,000 = 52 x 1,000 = 52 thousands. 520 thousands = 520,000; 52 hundreds = 5,200; 5 thousands 2 hundreds = 5,200.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: A warehouse has $42{,}600$ screws. They are packed in boxes of 100. How many boxes are filled?
questions.solution: 42,600 / 100 = 426, so 426 boxes are filled (there are 426 hundreds in 42,600).

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: What is the least five-digit number?
questions.solution: The first digit cannot be 0, so it is 1. The rest are 0. The least five-digit number is 10,000.

solve.work: The least five-digit number is 10,000 (9,999 has four digits).

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: What is the greatest five-digit number in which all five digits are different?
questions.solution: Use the five greatest digits, from greatest to least: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5. The number is 98,765.

solve.work: Use the greatest distinct digits in decreasing order: 9,8,7,6,5 -> 98,765.

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: Dana's five-digit number has a 3 in the ten-thousands place. The digit in the thousands place is twice that digit. All the other digits are 0. What is her number?
questions.solution: The thousands digit is 2 x 3 = 6. The number is 3 ten-thousands and 6 thousands: 36,000.

questions.skill: Find the number where a digit has a given value
questions.stem: In which number does the digit 4 have a value of $4{,}000$?
questions.solution: A 4 is worth 4,000 only in the thousands place. In 42,815 the 4 is in the ten-thousands place (40,000). In 28,415 it is in the hundreds place (400). In 28,154 it is in the ones place (4). In 24,815 it is in the thousands place, worth 4,000.

questions.skill: Build a number from place values that include zeros
questions.stem: A number has 3 ten-thousands, 0 thousands, 7 hundreds, 0 tens and 2 ones. What is the number?
questions.solution: Write the digits from the largest place to the smallest: 3, 0, 7, 0, 2. The number is 30,702.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: In $67{,}176$, the digit 7 appears twice. How much greater is the value of the first 7 (reading from the left) than the value of the second 7?
questions.solution: The first 7 is in the thousands place: 7,000. The second 7 is in the tens place: 70. The difference is 7,000 - 70 = 6,930.

solve.work: 67,176: 6 ten-thousands, 7 thousands, 1 hundred, 7 tens, 6 ones. First 7 = 7,000; second 7 = 70. Difference 7,000 - 70 = 6,930.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: In which number does the digit 8 have a greater value than the digit 5?
questions.solution: In 85,302 the 8 is worth 80,000 and the 5 is worth 5,000. In each other number the 5 is worth more than the 8.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a number
questions.stem: In $29{,}092$, the digit 9 appears twice. What is the total of the values of the two 9s?
questions.solution: One 9 is in the thousands place (9,000) and the other is in the tens place (90). Together: 9,000 + 90 = 9,090.

solve.work: 29,092: 2 ten-thousands, 9 thousands (9,000), 0 hundreds, 9 tens (90), 2 ones. Total 9,000 + 90 = 9,090.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: In which number is the digit in the thousands place exactly twice the digit in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: In 36,314 the thousands digit is 6 and the hundreds digit is 3, and 6 = 2 x 3. In the others the thousands digit is half, equal to, or four times the hundreds digit.

questions.skill: Digit in a given place
questions.stem: In $35{,}742$, swap the digit in the ten-thousands place with the digit in the hundreds place. What number do you get?
questions.solution: The ten-thousands digit is 3 and the hundreds digit is 7. Swapping them gives 7 (ten-thousands), 5, 3 (hundreds), 4, 2: 75,342.

solve.work: 35,742: ten-thousands 3, thousands 5, hundreds 7, tens 4, ones 2. Swap 3 and 7: ten-thousands 7, hundreds 3 -> 75,342.

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $3 \times 10{,}000 + 5 \times 1{,}000 + 4 \times 10 + 6$?
questions.solution: 3 x 10,000 = 30,000; 5 x 1,000 = 5,000; 4 x 10 = 40; plus 6. The total is 35,046 (there are no hundreds).

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.solution: Put the parts in order of place: 60,000 + 5,000 + 700 + 40 + 2 = 65,742.

questions.skill: Write a number from its parts (expanded form)
questions.stem: A number has 9 hundreds, 4 ten-thousands, 6 ones and 2 thousands, and no tens. What is the number?
questions.solution: Order the places from the left: 4 ten-thousands, 2 thousands, 9 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones. The number is 42,906.

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT equal to $45{,}230$?
questions.solution: 45,000 + 200 + 3 = 45,203, not 45,230. The other three each add up to 45,230.

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: The expanded form of a number is $50{,}000 + 6{,}000 + 90 + 4$. What is the sum of the digits of the number?
questions.solution: The number is 56,094. Its digits are 5, 6, 0, 9 and 4, and 5 + 6 + 0 + 9 + 4 = 24.

questions.skill: Write a number in expanded form
questions.stem: When a number is written in expanded form, you add the values of its digits that are not zero. Which number has exactly two numbers to add?
questions.solution: 30,200 = 30,000 + 200 (two parts). 12,345 has five parts, and 40,501 and 76,030 each have three.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: Which pair shows two names for the same number?
questions.solution: Forty-five thousand, six is 45,006. The others are 30,400, 12,305 and 8,090, which do not match 30,040, 12,035 and 80,090.

solve.work: eight thousand, ninety = 8,090 not 80,090. forty-five thousand, six = 45,006 (match). thirty thousand, four hundred = 30,400 not 30,040. twelve thousand, three hundred five = 12,305 not 12,035.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: What number is one more than sixty-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety-nine? Write your answer with digits.
questions.solution: Sixty-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety-nine is 69,999. One more is 70,000.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: In $70{,}070$, the first 7 (reading from the left) is worth how many times as much as the second 7?
questions.solution: The first 7 is worth 70,000 and the second 7 is worth 70. 70,000 / 70 = 1,000.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: In which number is the first 3 (reading from the left) worth exactly 10 times as much as the second 3?
questions.solution: In 33,415 the 3s are worth 30,000 and 3,000, and 30,000 is 10 times 3,000. In the others the first 3 is worth 100, 1,000 and 10,000 times the second.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: The digit 8 in $84{,}000$ is worth how many times as much as the digit 8 in $3{,}806$?
questions.solution: In 84,000 the 8 is worth 80,000. In 3,806 the 8 is in the hundreds place and is worth 800. 80,000 / 800 = 100.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: What is the least digit that can replace the box so that $3\square{,}250 > 38{,}640$ is true?
questions.solution: With the box as 9 we get 39,250, which is greater than 38,640. With 8 we get 38,250, which is less. So the least digit is 9.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: Which number is greater than $58{,}299$ and less than $58{,}310$?
questions.solution: 58,300 is greater than 58,299 and less than 58,310. 58,290 is too small and the other two are too big.

solve.work: Need 58,299 < n < 58,310. 58,320 too big; 58,290 too small; 58,300 works; 59,300 too big.

questions.skill: Compare two multi-digit numbers
questions.stem: The numbers $63{,}482$ and $63{,}187$ have the same digits in the first two places. Reading from the left, in which place do their digits first differ?
questions.solution: Ten-thousands: 6 and 6. Thousands: 3 and 3. Hundreds: 4 and 1. They first differ in the hundreds place (so 63,482 is greater).

solve.work: 63,482 vs 63,187: ten-thousands 6=6, thousands 3=3, hundreds 4 vs 1 differ first.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: The numbers $52{,}014$; $51{,}940$; $52{,}104$; $51{,}994$ and $52{,}041$ are put in order from least to greatest. Which number is in the middle?

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Sara has number cards $8{,}973$; $80{,}397$; $89{,}730$ and $8{,}397$. She lines them up starting with the greatest card. Which list shows her line?
questions.solution: The two 5-digit numbers come first: 89,730 > 80,397. Of the two 4-digit numbers, 8,973 > 8,397.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Using each of the digits 2, 5, 7, 0 and 9 exactly once, what is the least five-digit number you can make?
questions.solution: A number cannot start with 0, so the smallest first digit is 2. Then use the rest from least to greatest: 0, 5, 7, 9. The number is 20,579.

solve.work: Digits 0,2,5,7,9. First digit cannot be 0, so smallest nonzero 2 first, then 0,5,7,9: 20,579.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: A number has 18 thousands, 3 hundreds and 5 ones. What is the number?
questions.solution: 18 thousands is 18,000. Add 3 hundreds (300) and 5 ones: 18,305.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT another name for $47{,}300$?
questions.solution: 47 hundreds + 3 thousands = 4,700 + 3,000 = 7,700. The other three each equal 47,300.

solve.work: 47 thousands + 3 hundreds = 47,300. 4,730 tens = 47,300. 47 hundreds + 3 thousands = 4,700 + 3,000 = 7,700 (not). 473 hundreds = 47,300.

questions.skill: Name a number in different units (tens, hundreds, thousands)
questions.stem: What number is 7 ten-thousands plus 14 thousands?
questions.solution: 7 ten-thousands is 70,000 and 14 thousands is 14,000. 70,000 + 14,000 = 84,000.

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: I am a five-digit number. My ten-thousands digit is 6. My thousands digit is half of my ten-thousands digit. My hundreds digit is 0. My tens digit is 1 more than my thousands digit. My ones digit is 2 less than my ten-thousands digit. What number am I?
questions.solution: Ten-thousands 6; thousands 3 (half of 6); hundreds 0; tens 4 (3 + 1); ones 4 (6 - 2). The number is 63,044.

solve.work: Ten-thousands 6; thousands 6/2 = 3; hundreds 0; tens 3 + 1 = 4; ones 6 - 2 = 4. Number 63,044.

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: What is the least five-digit number that has a 7 in the thousands place and uses five different digits?
questions.solution: The ten-thousands digit cannot be 0, so the least choice is 1. The thousands digit is 7. Then use the least unused digits: 0 for the hundreds, 2 for the tens and 3 for the ones. The number is 17,023.

solve.work: Ten-thousands: least nonzero digit not 7 = 1. Thousands = 7. Remaining places smallest unused digits in order: 0, 2, 3. Number 17,023 (digits 1,7,0,2,3 all different).

questions.skill: Use place value to build or find a number
questions.stem: A number is greater than $50{,}000$ and less than $60{,}000$. The digit in its thousands place is 8 and the digit in its hundreds place is 0. Which could be the number?
questions.solution: Between 50,000 and 60,000 the first digit is 5. With thousands 8 and hundreds 0 we get 58,0__, so 58,052 fits.

solve.work: Must be 5x,xxx with thousands 8 and hundreds 0: 58,0xx. 58,502 has hundreds 5; 58,052 fits; 85,042 > 60,000; 50,805 has thousands 0.

questions.skill: Value of each digit
questions.stem: The digit in the thousands place and the digit in the hundreds place of $36{,}420$ are swapped, making a new number. How much less than $36{,}420$ is the new number?
questions.solution: The 6 is in the thousands place and the 4 is in the hundreds place. Swapping them gives $34{,}620$. The difference is $36{,}420 - 34{,}620 = 1{,}800$. Check by place value: the 6 loses 5,400 of value (6,000 down to 600), and the 4 gains 3,600 (400 up to 4,000), so the number drops by 1,800.

questions.skill: Number names (word form) and standard form
questions.stem: Which number is written in words as seventy thousand, three hundred two?
questions.solution: Seventy thousand is 70,000, three hundred is 300 and two is 2. Put together, that is 70,302. The ten-thousands place holds the 7, the thousands place holds a 0, and the tens place holds a 0.

questions.skill: Add two 4-digit numbers
questions.solution: Add each place, starting with the ones: 6 + 3 = 9, 2 + 7 = 9, 3 + 5 = 8, 4 + 2 = 6. No place needs regrouping, so the sum is 6,899.

questions.skill: Subtract two 4-digit numbers
questions.solution: Subtract each place, starting with the ones: 5 - 2 = 3, 6 - 4 = 2, 4 - 1 = 3, 8 - 3 = 5. The difference is 5,323.

questions.skill: Add with regrouping in a word problem
questions.stem: A school collected 1,250 cans in May and 1,375 cans in June. How many cans did it collect in all?
questions.solution: Add: 1,250 + 1,375. Ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Tens: 5 + 7 = 12, so write 2 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. Thousands: 1 + 1 = 2. The total is 2,625. (2,525 forgets the regrouped hundred.)

questions.skill: Add multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Find the sum of $3{,}475$ and $1{,}218$.
questions.solution: Ones: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 1 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 4 + 2 = 6. Thousands: 3 + 1 = 4. The sum is 4,693.

solve.work: 3,475 + 1,218: ones 5+8=13 (write 3, carry 1); tens 7+1+1=9; hundreds 4+2=6; thousands 3+1=4. Sum 4,693.

questions.skill: Add multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Which is the sum of $6{,}250$ and $2{,}875$?
questions.solution: Ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Tens: 5 + 7 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 2 + 8 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 thousand. Thousands: 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. The sum is 9,125.

questions.skill: Add multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.solution: No place needs regrouping: 14,200 + 3,500 = 17,700.

questions.skill: Subtract multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.solution: Ones: 0 - 5 needs regrouping: 10 - 5 = 5 (tens now 3). Tens: 3 - 1 = 2. Hundreds: 5 - 2 = 3. Thousands: 7 - 3 = 4. The answer is 4,325.

questions.skill: Subtract multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Find the difference: $5{,}362 - 1{,}148$.
questions.solution: Ones: 2 - 8 needs regrouping: 12 - 8 = 4. Tens: 5 - 4 = 1. Hundreds: 3 - 1 = 2. Thousands: 5 - 1 = 4. The difference is 4,214.

questions.skill: Subtract multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: How much is $28{,}600$ minus $4{,}200$?
questions.solution: No regrouping is needed: 28,600 - 4,200 = 24,400.

questions.skill: Subtract from a number with zeros
questions.solution: Regroup 5,000 as 4 thousands and 10 hundreds. Then 10 hundreds - 2 hundreds = 8 hundreds, and 4 thousands - 1 thousand = 3 thousands. The answer is 3,800.

questions.skill: Subtract from a number with zeros
questions.stem: Which is the value of $3{,}000 - 1{,}450$?
questions.solution: Regroup 3 thousands as 2 thousands and 10 hundreds, then one hundred as 10 tens. Subtracting gives 3,000 - 1,450 = 1,550.

questions.stem: A farm picked $2{,}340$ apples on Monday and $1{,}860$ apples on Tuesday. How many apples did it pick in all?
questions.solution: Add the two days: 2,340 + 1,860 = 4,200.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step add and subtract problem

questions.skill: Solve a two-step add and subtract problem
questions.stem: A bus carried $3{,}200$ riders on Monday and $2{,}800$ riders on Tuesday. Of all those riders, $1{,}000$ were children. How many riders were not children?
questions.solution: 3,200 + 2,800 = 6,000 riders in all. Then 6,000 - 1,000 = 5,000 were not children.

questions.skill: Find a missing number in an addition or subtraction sentence
questions.stem: $4{,}300 + \square = 9{,}800$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: Subtract to find the missing addend: 9,800 - 4,300 = 5,500.

questions.skill: Find a missing number in an addition or subtraction sentence
questions.stem: A number minus $1{,}200$ equals $3{,}400$. What is the number?
questions.solution: Add back what was taken away: 3,400 + 1,200 = 4,600.

questions.skill: Understand regrouping in the algorithm
questions.stem: When adding the ones in $3{,}478 + 1{,}256$, we get $8 + 6 = 14$. How many ones are written in the ones place of the answer?
questions.solution: 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. Write 4 in the ones place and regroup the 1 ten.

solve.work: 14 ones = 1 ten and 4 ones: write 4 in the ones place, regroup the ten.

questions.skill: Understand regrouping in the algorithm
questions.stem: In $2{,}365 + 1{,}748$, the ones add up to 13 ones. How is 13 ones regrouped?
questions.solution: 10 ones make 1 ten, so 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones.

questions.skill: Understand regrouping in the algorithm
questions.stem: To subtract $4{,}325 - 1{,}647$, you cannot take 7 ones from 5 ones. So you regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. How many ones are there after regrouping?
questions.solution: 5 ones + 10 ones = 15 ones, and now 15 - 7 can be done.

solve.work: 4,325 has 2 tens and 5 ones. Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 + 10 = 15 ones.

questions.skill: Connect earlier strategies to the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Rosa finds $2{,}413 + 3{,}265$ by adding each place separately: $2{,}000 + 3{,}000$, $400 + 200$, $10 + 60$ and $3 + 5$. What is the total of the four partial sums?
questions.solution: The partial sums are 5,000; 600; 70 and 8. Their total is 5,678.

questions.skill: Connect earlier strategies to the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Ben adds $3{,}500 + 2{,}400$ by first finding $3{,}500 + 2{,}000 = 5{,}500$. What should he do next?
questions.solution: 2,400 is 2,000 + 400. He has added the 2,000, so he still has to add the 400 to 5,500 to get 5,900.

solve.work: 2,400 = 2,000 + 400. After adding 2,000, add the remaining 400 to 5,500: 5,900.

questions.skill: Connect earlier strategies to the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Kai finds how far $4{,}800$ is from $5{,}300$ by counting up: from $4{,}800$ to $5{,}000$, and then from $5{,}000$ to $5{,}300$. How much did he count up in all?
questions.solution: 4,800 to 5,000 is 200, and 5,000 to 5,300 is 300. In all he counted up 500.

questions.skill: Find and fix a mistake in a calculation
questions.stem: Dev worked out $3{,}456 + 2{,}789$ and got $5{,}245$. What mistake did he most likely make?
choices: He forgot to add the 1 regrouped from the hundreds into the thousands.
He forgot to regroup the ones into the tens.
He wrote the ones digit in the tens place.
He subtracted the thousands instead of adding them.
questions.answer: He forgot to add the 1 regrouped from the hundreds into the thousands.
questions.solution: The correct sum is 6,245. Dev's thousands digit is 5 = 3 + 2, so he left out the 1 regrouped from the hundreds (4 + 7 + 1 = 12).

solve.answer: He forgot to add the 1 regrouped from the hundreds into the thousands.
solve.work: Correct: 3,456 + 2,789 = 6,245. Dev's 5,245 is 1,000 short. Hundreds 4+7+1=12 -> carry 1 thousand; omitting it gives thousands 3+2=5. (Forgetting the ones regroup would give 6,235.)

questions.stem: Which equation is correct?
questions.solution: Hundreds: 5 + 8 = 13 hundreds, which is 1 thousand and 3 hundreds. Thousands: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. So the sum is 4,300.

questions.solution: Ones: 2 + 9 = 11, write 1, regroup 1. Tens: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10, write 0, regroup 1. Hundreds: 4 + 6 + 1 = 11, write 1, regroup 1. Thousands: 7 + 5 + 1 = 13, write 3, regroup 1. Ten-thousands: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. The sum is 63,101.

questions.solution: Subtract the filled seats from all the seats: 45,380 - 28,947 = 16,433. Check: 28,947 + 16,433 = 45,380. (74,327 comes from adding instead, and 23,647 from taking the smaller digit from the larger in every column.)

questions.skill: Add multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Use the standard algorithm to add $46{,}387 + 28{,}549$. What is the sum?
questions.solution: Ones: 7 + 9 = 16, write 6, regroup 1. Tens: 8 + 4 + 1 = 13, write 3, regroup 1. Hundreds: 3 + 5 + 1 = 9. Thousands: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4, regroup 1. Ten-thousands: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. The sum is 74,936.

questions.skill: Add multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Add $35{,}968$ and $4{,}739$. Which answer is correct?
questions.solution: Ones: 8 + 9 = 17, write 7, regroup 1. Tens: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10, write 0, regroup 1. Hundreds: 9 + 7 + 1 = 17, write 7, regroup 1. Thousands: 5 + 4 + 1 = 10, write 0, regroup 1. Ten-thousands: 3 + 1 = 4. The sum is 40,707.

questions.skill: Add multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Line up the digits by place value and add: $19{,}875 + 52{,}648$.
questions.solution: Ones: 5 + 8 = 13. Tens: 7 + 4 + 1 = 12. Hundreds: 8 + 6 + 1 = 15. Thousands: 9 + 2 + 1 = 12. Ten-thousands: 1 + 5 + 1 = 7. The sum is 72,523.

questions.skill: Subtract multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Use the standard algorithm to subtract: $63{,}214 - 28{,}857$.
questions.solution: Ones: 14 - 7 = 7. Tens: 0 - 5 needs regrouping: 10 - 5 = 5. Hundreds: 1 - 8 needs regrouping: 11 - 8 = 3. Thousands: 2 - 8 needs regrouping: 12 - 8 = 4. Ten-thousands: 5 - 2 = 3. The answer is 34,357.

questions.solution: The difference is the greater number minus the lesser: 55,421 - 19,768 = 35,653.

questions.solution: Regroup across the zeros: 40,000 is 3 ten-thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones. Then 40,000 - 17,356 = 22,644. Check: 22,644 + 17,356 = 40,000.

questions.solution: After the first regrouping there are 10 tens. Moving 1 ten to the ones place leaves 9 tens.

solve.work: 7,205: 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones. Regroup 1 hundred: 1 hundred, 10 tens. Regroup 1 ten: 9 tens, 15 ones. 9 tens left.

questions.stem: Adding $4{,}725 + 3{,}617$ by partial sums, the hundreds give $700 + 600 = 1{,}300$. In the standard algorithm, what is done with these 13 hundreds?
choices: Write 3 in the hundreds place and regroup 1 thousand.

questions.answer: Write 3 in the hundreds place and regroup 1 thousand.
questions.solution: 13 hundreds is 1 thousand and 3 hundreds: write 3 in the hundreds place and add the 1 thousand to the thousands column.

solve.work: 4,725 + 3,617: ones 12 (carry 1 ten), tens 2+1+1=4, hundreds 7+6=13 hundreds = 1 thousand 3 hundreds: write 3, regroup 1 thousand.

questions.solution: 8,000 - 5,000 = 3,000. Taking away 3 less means 3 more is left: 3,003.

questions.stem: Pat finds $5{,}380 + 2{,}475$ by thinking $5{,}380 + 2{,}000 = 7{,}380$, then $7{,}380 + 400 = 7{,}780$, then adding the rest. What is the sum?
questions.solution: The rest is 75: 7,780 + 75 = 7,855. Check with the algorithm: 5,380 + 2,475 = 7,855.

questions.skill: Find and fix a mistake in a calculation
questions.stem: Leo wrote $52{,}000 - 17{,}348 = 45{,}348$. What mistake did he make?
choices: He forgot to subtract the thousands.
In each place he subtracted the smaller digit from the larger digit instead of regrouping.
He added the digits in the ones place.
He regrouped but forgot to write the regrouped ten.
questions.answer: In each place he subtracted the smaller digit from the larger digit instead of regrouping.
questions.solution: The correct answer is 34,652. Leo found the difference of the two digits in each place (4, 5, 3, 4, 8) instead of regrouping.

solve.answer: In each place he subtracted the smaller digit from the larger digit instead of regrouping.
solve.work: Correct 52,000 - 17,348 = 34,652. Leo: 5-1=4, then |2-7|=5, |0-3|=3, |0-4|=4, |0-8|=8 -> 45,348, i.e. smaller digit from larger in each place.

questions.skill: Find and fix a mistake in a calculation
questions.stem: Ana found $39{,}406 + 24{,}685 = 64{,}081$, but she made a mistake. What is the correct sum?
questions.solution: Ones: 6 + 5 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 0 + 8 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 4 + 6 = 10, write 0 and regroup. Thousands: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14. Ten-thousands: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. The sum is 64,091.

questions.skill: Find and fix a mistake in a calculation
questions.stem: Tara added $3{,}482 + 215$ and got $5{,}632$. What mistake did she most likely make?
choices: She forgot to regroup the ones.
She left out the ones when adding.
She lined up the digits from the left instead of by place value.
questions.answer: She lined up the digits from the left instead of by place value.
questions.solution: The correct sum is 3,697. Tara got 3,482 + 2,150 = 5,632, so 215 was written as 2,150, with its digits lined up from the left.

solve.answer: She lined up the digits from the left instead of by place value.
solve.work: Correct 3,482 + 215 = 3,697. Lining up from the left treats 215 as 2,150: 3,482 + 2,150 = 5,632, Tara's answer.

questions.solution: Subtract the new books: 41,230 - 8,675 = 32,555.

questions.skill: Understand regrouping in the algorithm
questions.stem: How many times do you need to regroup (carry) when you add $68{,}764 + 27{,}359$ with the standard algorithm?
questions.solution: Ones: 4 + 9 = 13 (carry). Tens: 6 + 5 + 1 = 12 (carry). Hundreds: 7 + 3 + 1 = 11 (carry). Thousands: 8 + 7 + 1 = 16 (carry). Ten-thousands: 6 + 2 + 1 = 9 (no carry). That is 4 carries.

solve.work: 68,764 + 27,359: ones 4+9=13 (carry); tens 6+5+1=12 (carry); hundreds 7+3+1=11 (carry); thousands 8+7+1=16 (carry); ten-thousands 6+2+1=9 (no carry). 4 regroupings; sum 96,123.

questions.skill: Understand regrouping in the algorithm
questions.stem: Mr. Cruz subtracts $40{,}000 - 12{,}345$ with the standard algorithm. He regroups from the left, one place at a time, until the ones place has enough to subtract from. After all the regrouping, how many ones are in the ones place?
questions.solution: 40,000 becomes 3 ten-thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones. So there are 10 ones.

solve.work: 40,000: 4 ten-thousands -> 3 and 10 thousands; 10 thousands -> 9 and 10 hundreds; 10 hundreds -> 9 and 10 tens; 10 tens -> 9 and 10 ones. Ones place has 10.

questions.skill: Understand regrouping in the algorithm
questions.stem: When adding $9{,}876 + 5{,}432$ with the standard algorithm, starting at the ones, which is the first place where you need to regroup?
questions.solution: Ones: 6 + 2 = 8, no regrouping. Tens: 7 + 3 = 10, so you regroup here.

solve.work: 9,876 + 5,432: ones 6+2=8 (no regroup); tens 7+3=10 (regroup). First regroup at tens.

questions.skill: Connect earlier strategies to the standard algorithm
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $48{,}250 - 19{,}999$?
questions.solution: 19,999 is 1 less than 20,000. Taking away 1 less leaves 1 more, so 48,250 - 19,999 = 48,250 - 20,000 + 1.

solve.work: 19,999 = 20,000 - 1, so subtracting 19,999 = subtracting 20,000 then adding 1 back: 48,250 - 20,000 + 1 = 28,251.

questions.skill: Find and fix a mistake in a calculation

questions.solution: 33,217 + 49,785 = 83,002, not 82,002. The other three equations are correct.

questions.skill: Find and fix a mistake in a calculation
questions.stem: Priya found $71{,}000 - 35{,}480 = 35{,}520$. Which addition checks her answer?
questions.solution: Subtraction is checked by adding the answer to the number taken away: 35,520 + 35,480 = 71,000, so her answer is right.

solve.work: Check a difference by adding it to the number subtracted: 35,520 + 35,480 = 71,000. Only the last option is an addition of that form (and it is true).

questions.skill: Find and fix a mistake in a calculation
questions.stem: A student found $36{,}859 + 27{,}574 = 64{,}423$. How much too small is the student's answer?
questions.solution: 36,859 + 27,574 = 64,433. The student's answer is 64,423, which is 10 too small (for example, the 1 regrouped from the ones may have been left out of the tens).

questions.skill: Multiplication fact fluency
questions.stem: What is $7 \times 8$?
questions.solution: 7 groups of 8 is 56, so $7 \times 8 = 56$.

questions.skill: Identify a prime number
questions.stem: Which of these numbers is prime?
questions.solution: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 21 = 3 x 7, 33 = 3 x 11 and 39 = 3 x 13, so they are composite. 29 cannot be made by multiplying two smaller whole numbers, so 29 is prime.

solve.work: 21 = 3 x 7, 33 = 3 x 11, 39 = 3 x 13 are composite; 29 has only factors 1 and 29, so prime.

questions.skill: Identify a multiple
questions.stem: Which of these numbers is a multiple of 7?
questions.solution: Multiples of 7 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63. Only 35 is in the list: 7 x 5 = 35.

solve.work: 35 = 7 x 5. 57 = 3 x 19, 37 prime, 53 prime: not multiples of 7.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which of these is a factor of 18?
questions.solution: $18 \div 6 = 3$ with nothing left over, so 6 is a factor of 18. Dividing 18 by 4, 5 or 8 always leaves a remainder.

solve.work: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Of 8, 6, 4, 5 only 6 divides 18 (18 = 6 x 3).

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: A factor pair of 24 is 4 and another number. What is the other number?
questions.solution: A factor pair multiplies to 24. Since $4 \times 6 = 24$, the other number is $24 \div 4 = 6$. The choice 20 subtracts, 28 adds and 96 multiplies by 4.

solve.work: 24 / 4 = 6, so 4 and 6 is a factor pair.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: How many factors does 10 have?
questions.solution: The factors of 10 are 1, 2, 5 and 10, because $1 \times 10 = 10$ and $2 \times 5 = 10$. That is 4 factors.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which pair of numbers is a factor pair of 16?
questions.solution: A factor pair multiplies to 16, and $2 \times 8 = 16$. The other pairs add up to 16 but do not multiply to 16: $6 \times 10 = 60$, $4 \times 12 = 48$ and $5 \times 11 = 55$.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Eli makes a rectangle from 30 square tiles. Each row has 6 tiles, and every row is full. How many rows does he make?
questions.solution: The 30 tiles are in equal rows of 6, so the number of rows is $30 \div 6 = 5$. Check: $6 \times 5 = 30$, so 6 and 5 are a factor pair of 30.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which number is composite?
questions.solution: $15 = 3 \times 5$, so 15 has factors besides 1 and itself. That makes it composite. The numbers 7, 11 and 13 each have only the factors 1 and themselves, so they are prime.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which sentence describes a prime number?
choices: A number greater than 1 whose only factors are 1 and itself
A number with exactly three factors
Any number greater than 1 that ends in 1, 3, 7 or 9
questions.answer: A number greater than 1 whose only factors are 1 and itself
questions.solution: A prime number is greater than 1 and has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. Not every odd number is prime (9 is not), and neither is every number ending in 1, 3, 7 or 9 (21 is not).

solve.answer: A number greater than 1 whose only factors are 1 and itself
solve.work: Definition of prime: greater than 1, only factors 1 and itself. Odd numbers like 9, numbers ending in 1 like 21, and numbers with 3 factors like 9 are not all prime.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.solution: The number 1 is not prime, because it has only one factor. The number 2 has exactly two factors, 1 and 2, so 2 is the smallest prime number.

solve.work: 1 is not prime; 2 has factors 1 and 2 only. Smallest prime is 2.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Is 9 prime or composite?
choices: Prime, because it is a square number
Neither prime nor composite, because it is odd
questions.solution: 9 has the factors 1, 3 and 9. Since it has a factor other than 1 and itself, it is composite. Being odd does not make a number prime.

solve.work: 9 = 3 x 3, so it has factor 3 besides 1 and 9: composite.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of 6?
questions.solution: The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, and so on, and $6 \times 3 = 18$. The numbers 16, 21 and 27 are not on that list.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: Write the multiples of 4 in order: 4, 8, 12, and so on. What is the fifth number in this list?
questions.solution: The list is 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. The fifth number is $5 \times 4 = 20$.

questions.skill: Multiples

questions.solution: Each number is 5 more than the one before, so the next number is $20 + 5 = 25$.

questions.solution: "3 times as many" means 3 groups of 4: $3 \times 4 = 12$ stickers.

questions.solution: $5 \times 6 = 30$ says that 30 is 5 groups of 6, so 30 is 5 times as large as 6. "More than" describes adding, not multiplying.

solve.work: 5 x 6 = 30 reads as 30 is 5 times as large as 6.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: A dog weighs 30 pounds. This is 5 times as much as a cat weighs. How many pounds does the cat weigh?
questions.solution: The dog weighs 5 times as much as the cat, so the cat weighs $30 \div 5 = 6$ pounds. The choice 25 subtracts 5, 35 adds 5, and 150 multiplies by 5.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: Mia has 2 pencils. Lee has 10 pencils. Lee has how many times as many pencils as Mia?
questions.solution: Divide to compare: $10 \div 2 = 5$. Lee has 5 times as many pencils as Mia.

questions.solution: $6 \times 15 = 6 \times 10 + 6 \times 5 = 60 + 30 = 90$ seats.

questions.solution: 3 bags use $3 \times 5 = 15$ cookies. A fourth bag would need 20. The cookies left over are $17 - 15 = 2$.

questions.skill: Remainders
questions.stem: What is the remainder when 23 is divided by 4?
questions.solution: $4 \times 5 = 20$ and $23 - 20 = 3$. So $23 \div 4 = 5$ remainder 3. The choice 5 is the quotient.

questions.skill: Remainders
questions.stem: A baker has 29 muffins. She fills as many boxes as she can with exactly 6 muffins in each box. How many muffins are left over?
questions.solution: $29 \div 6 = 4$ with a remainder of 5, because $4 \times 6 = 24$ and $29 - 24 = 5$. She fills 4 boxes and has 5 muffins left over.

questions.skill: Division with a remainder in context
questions.stem: A baker puts 8 muffins in each box. She has 75 muffins. How many boxes can she fill completely?
questions.solution: 75 divided by 8 is 9 with a remainder of 3, because 8 x 9 = 72 and 75 - 72 = 3. The 3 left-over muffins do not fill a box, so she fills 9 boxes.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison: find the smaller amount
questions.stem: A red ribbon is 36 centimeters long. It is 4 times as long as a blue ribbon. How long is the blue ribbon, in centimeters?
questions.solution: "4 times as long" means red = 4 x blue. So blue = 36 divided by 4 = 9 centimeters. Check: 4 x 9 = 36. (144 multiplies instead, 32 subtracts 4 and 40 adds 4.)

solve.work: Red = 4 x blue, so blue = 36 / 4 = 9 cm.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: How many different factors does 28 have?
questions.solution: Find the factor pairs of 28: $1 \times 28$, $2 \times 14$ and $4 \times 7$. The factors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and 28, which is 6 factors.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which list shows all of the factors of 14?
questions.solution: The factor pairs of 14 are $1 \times 14$ and $2 \times 7$, so the factors are 1, 2, 7 and 14. One wrong list leaves out 1, one leaves out 14, and 4 is not a factor of 14.

solve.work: 14 = 1 x 14 = 2 x 7, so factors 1, 2, 7, 14. 4 is not a factor; the other lists miss 1 or 14.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which number is NOT a factor of 40?
questions.solution: $40 \div 5 = 8$, $40 \div 8 = 5$ and $40 \div 10 = 4$ leave nothing over, so 5, 8 and 10 are factors of 40. $40 \div 12$ leaves a remainder of 4, so 12 is not a factor.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 30?
questions.solution: Check each number: 21 = 3 × 7, 22 is even, 23 is prime, 24 is even, 25 = 5 × 5, 26 is even, 27 = 3 × 9, 28 is even and 29 is prime. Only 23 and 29 are prime, so the answer is 2.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which list has only prime numbers?
questions.solution: 11, 13, 17 and 19 each have only the factors 1 and themselves. In the other lists, 15 = 3 × 5, 9 = 3 × 3 and 21 = 3 × 7 are composite.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Maya says that 51 is prime. Which fact shows that she is wrong?
questions.solution: A prime number has no factors besides 1 and itself. Since $3 \times 17 = 51$, the number 3 is a factor of 51, so 51 is composite. Every number equals 1 times itself, so $1 \times 51 = 51$ proves nothing.

solve.work: 3 x 17 = 51 shows a factor other than 1 and 51, so 51 is composite.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: What is the only prime number between 30 and 34?
questions.solution: The numbers between 30 and 34 are 31, 32 and 33. 32 is even, and $33 = 3 \times 11$. The number 31 has only the factors 1 and 31, so it is prime.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: What is the least multiple of 9 that is greater than 50?
questions.solution: Count by 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54. The number 45 is below 50, and the first multiple above 50 is $9 \times 6 = 54$. The choice 59 adds 9 to 50, and 63 is the multiple after 54.

solve.work: Multiples of 9: 45, 54, 63. Least above 50 is 54. 59 is not a multiple.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: Which list shows only multiples of 8?
questions.solution: The multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, and so on. Each other list has a number that is not a multiple of 8: 20, 18, or 4 and 12.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: A store sells eggs in cartons of 12. Dan buys some cartons and gets more than 50 eggs but fewer than 70 eggs. How many eggs does Dan get?
questions.solution: The number of eggs is a multiple of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72. Only 60 is more than 50 and fewer than 70. Dan buys 5 cartons.

solve.work: Multiples of 12: 48, 60, 72. Only 60 is between 50 and 70 (5 cartons).

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of both 3 and 4?
questions.solution: $24 = 3 \times 8$ and $24 = 4 \times 6$, so 24 is a multiple of both. The number 18 is a multiple of 3 only, 20 of 4 only, and 21 of 3 only.

solve.work: 24 = 3 x 8 = 4 x 6. 21 not by 4, 20 not by 3, 18 not by 4.

questions.skill: Multiplication and division facts to 10 x 10

questions.solution: There are 9 rows with 7 muffins in each, so $9 \times 7 = 63$ muffins.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: On a sunny day a bakery sells 8 times as many muffins as on a rainy day. On the rainy day it sold 17 muffins. How many muffins does it sell on the sunny day?
questions.solution: The sunny day is 8 times the rainy day: $17 \times 8 = 136$ muffins.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: A tree is 36 feet tall. A shrub is 4 feet tall. Which sentence is true?
choices: The tree is 32 times as tall as the shrub
The tree is 9 times as tall as the shrub
The tree is 9 feet taller than the shrub
The shrub is 9 times as tall as the tree
questions.answer: The tree is 9 times as tall as the shrub
questions.solution: $36 \div 4 = 9$, so the tree is 9 times as tall as the shrub. The difference, $36 - 4 = 32$, is how many feet taller the tree is, not how many times as tall.

solve.answer: The tree is 9 times as tall as the shrub
solve.work: 36 / 4 = 9, so the tree is 9 times as tall as the shrub (and 32 feet taller).

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: Which equation can be used to find how many times as large 56 is as 8?
questions.solution: "56 is $n$ times as large as 8" means 56 is $n$ groups of 8, so $8 \times n = 56$. Then $n = 56 \div 8 = 7$. The equation $8 + n = 56$ would mean 56 is $n$ more than 8.

solve.work: How many times as large: 8 x n = 56 (n = 7). n / 56 = 8 gives 448; 8 + n is additive; 56 x 8 is a product.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: A rope is 72 inches long. A string is 9 inches long. The rope is how many times as long as the string?
questions.solution: $72 \div 9 = 8$, so the rope is 8 times as long as the string.

questions.stem: A baker has 50 cupcakes. Each tray holds 9 cupcakes. How many trays are needed to hold all the cupcakes?
questions.solution: $9 \times 5 = 45$, so 5 full trays hold 45 cupcakes and 5 are left over. Those need another tray, so $5 + 1 = 6$ trays are needed.

solve.work: 50 = 9 x 5 + 5, so 5 full trays plus one for the last 5: 6 trays.

questions.skill: Remainders
questions.stem: Which of these cannot be the remainder when a whole number is divided by 5?
questions.solution: A remainder is always less than the divisor. If 5 were left over, another group of 5 could be made. So 5 cannot be a remainder when dividing by 5.

solve.work: Remainders on dividing by 5 are 0 to 4; 5 cannot be one.

questions.skill: Four-digit by one-digit quotient with a zero
questions.stem: What is $3{,}648 \div 6$?
questions.solution: 6 x 600 = 3,600, and 3,648 - 3,600 = 48. Then 48 divided by 6 is 8. So the quotient is 600 + 8 = 608. Check: 6 x 608 = 3,648.

questions.skill: Count the factor pairs of a number
questions.stem: A factor pair is two whole numbers that multiply to make a number. The order does not matter, so $2 \times 18$ and $18 \times 2$ are the same pair. How many factor pairs does 36 have?
questions.solution: The factor pairs of 36 are 1 x 36, 2 x 18, 3 x 12, 4 x 9 and 6 x 6. That is 5 pairs. (6 x 6 counts as one pair.)

solve.work: Pairs for 36: 1x36, 2x18, 3x12, 4x9, 6x6. 5 does not divide 36. That is 5 pairs (6x6 counts, as two whole numbers 6 and 6 multiply to 36).

questions.skill: Interpret a remainder
questions.stem: A school trip has 150 students. Each bus seats 40 students. What is the fewest number of buses needed so that every student has a seat?
questions.solution: 150 divided by 40 is 3 with a remainder of 30. Three buses seat 120 students, and 30 students are left without a seat, so one more bus is needed. The fewest number of buses is 4.

solve.work: 150 / 40 = 3 remainder 30; 3 buses seat 120, so 30 students need a 4th bus. 4.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Dee lists the factor pairs of 30 and does not repeat a pair. How many pairs are on her list?
questions.solution: The pairs are $1 \times 30$, $2 \times 15$, $3 \times 10$ and $5 \times 6$. That is 4 pairs. The choice 8 counts each factor on its own instead of each pair.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: What is the sum of all the factors of 12?
questions.solution: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. Their sum is $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 12 = 28$.

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which number has exactly three factors?
questions.solution: The factors of 9 are 1, 3 and 9, which is exactly three. The factors of 10 are 1, 2, 5, 10 (four), of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 (six), and of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15 (four).

questions.skill: Factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: What is the largest factor of 54 that is less than 20?
questions.solution: The factor pairs of 54 are $1 \times 54$, $2 \times 27$, $3 \times 18$ and $6 \times 9$. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, 27 and 54. The largest one below 20 is 18.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which statement about the number 1 is true?
choices: It is prime, because it is the smallest number
It is composite, because it divides every number
It is both prime and composite
It is neither prime nor composite
questions.answer: It is neither prime nor composite
questions.solution: A prime has exactly two factors and a composite has more than two. The number 1 has only one factor, itself, so it is neither prime nor composite.

solve.answer: It is neither prime nor composite
solve.work: 1 has only one factor, so it is neither prime nor composite.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: What is the sum of the two prime numbers between 10 and 14?
questions.solution: The numbers between 10 and 14 are 11, 12 and 13. 12 is composite, and 11 and 13 are prime. Their sum is $11 + 13 = 24$.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which of these odd numbers is composite?
questions.solution: $57 = 3 \times 19$ (the digits add up to 12, so 3 divides it), so 57 is composite. The numbers 53, 59 and 61 have no factors other than 1 and themselves.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: What is the smallest number greater than 0 that is a multiple of both 6 and 9?
questions.solution: The multiples of 9 are 9, 18, 27, ... and the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, ... The first number on both lists is 18.

solve.work: Multiples of 9: 9, 18; 18 = 6 x 3. Least common multiple 18.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: How many multiples of 7 are there from 1 to 50?
questions.solution: The multiples of 7 up to 50 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 and 49. The next one, 56, is more than 50. That is 7 multiples.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: Which number is NOT a multiple of 9?
questions.solution: $9 \times 6 = 54$, $9 \times 7 = 63$ and $9 \times 8 = 72$. The multiples of 9 go 72, 81, so 75 is not one of them.

questions.skill: Multiples
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 9 and adds 9 each time: 9, 18, 27, and so on. What is the 11th number in the pattern?
questions.solution: The numbers in the pattern are the multiples of 9, so the 11th number is $9 \times 11 = 99$. The choice 90 is the 10th number, 108 is the 12th, and 20 is $9 + 11$.

solve.work: nth number is 9 x n; 11th is 99.

questions.skill: Multiplication and division facts to 10 x 10
questions.stem: What is $7 \times 8 - 6 \times 6$?
questions.solution: Work out each product first: $7 \times 8 = 56$ and $6 \times 6 = 36$. Then $56 - 36 = 20$.

questions.skill: Multiplication and division facts to 10 x 10
questions.stem: Which expression does NOT equal 48?
questions.solution: $6 \times 8 = 48$, $4 \times 12 = 48$ and $3 \times 16 = 48$. But $7 \times 7 = 49$.

questions.skill: Multiplication and division facts to 10 x 10
questions.stem: Four times a number is 36. What is six times the same number?
questions.solution: The number is $36 \div 4 = 9$. Six times that number is $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: A skyscraper is 9 times as tall as a house. The house is 24 feet tall. How many feet taller is the skyscraper than the house?
questions.solution: The skyscraper is $9 \times 24 = 216$ feet tall. It is taller than the house by $216 - 24 = 192$ feet. The choice 216 is the skyscraper's height, not the difference.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: Nina has 3 times as many marbles as Omar, and Omar has 4 times as many marbles as Pat. Pat has 7 marbles. How many marbles does Nina have?
questions.solution: Omar has $4 \times 7 = 28$ marbles. Nina has $3 \times 28 = 84$ marbles.

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: Ravi has 6 stickers. Tess has 24 stickers. Which sentence is true?
choices: Tess has 18 more stickers than Ravi, and 6 times as many
Tess has 18 more stickers than Ravi, and 4 times as many
Tess has 30 more stickers than Ravi, and 4 times as many
Tess has 4 more stickers than Ravi, and 18 times as many
questions.answer: Tess has 18 more stickers than Ravi, and 4 times as many
questions.solution: The difference is $24 - 6 = 18$, so Tess has 18 more stickers. The comparison by multiplying is $24 \div 6 = 4$, so she has 4 times as many. Both parts must be right.

solve.answer: Tess has 18 more stickers than Ravi, and 4 times as many

questions.skill: Multiplicative comparison
questions.stem: A red pole is 120 centimeters tall. It is 8 times as tall as a green pole. A yellow pole is 3 times as tall as the green pole. How tall is the yellow pole, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The green pole is $120 \div 8 = 15$ centimeters tall. The yellow pole is $3 \times 15 = 45$ centimeters tall.

questions.skill: Multi-digit products
questions.stem: What is $48 \times 36$?

questions.skill: Multi-digit products
questions.stem: What is $3{,}406 \times 5$?

questions.skill: Multi-digit products
questions.stem: A printing press prints $2{,}450$ pages each hour. How many pages does it print in 8 hours?

questions.skill: Multi-digit products
questions.stem: Which product is the greatest?
questions.solution: Work out each product: $4 \times 620 = 2{,}480$, $5 \times 480 = 2{,}400$, $6 \times 390 = 2{,}340$ and $7 \times 330 = 2{,}310$. The greatest is $4 \times 620$.

questions.skill: Multi-digit products
questions.stem: A school orders 24 boxes of markers. Each box has 36 markers. How many markers is that in all?
questions.solution: $24 \times 30 = 720$ and $24 \times 6 = 144$. Add: $720 + 144 = 864$. The choice 720 leaves out the ones digit, and 60 adds the numbers.

questions.skill: Multi-digit quotients
questions.stem: What is $5{,}635 \div 7$?
questions.solution: $5{,}600 \div 7 = 800$ and $35 \div 7 = 5$. Add: $800 + 5 = 805$. The tens place has a zero in the quotient. Check: $7 \times 805 = 5{,}635$.

questions.skill: Multi-digit quotients
questions.stem: A library puts $2{,}415$ books equally onto 5 shelves. How many books are on each shelf?

questions.skill: Multi-digit quotients
questions.stem: Which quotient is the greatest?

questions.skill: Multi-digit quotients
questions.stem: A number divided by 7 is 126. What is the number?
questions.solution: Undo the division by multiplying: $126 \times 7 = 882$. Check: $882 \div 7 = 126$.

questions.skill: Remainders
questions.stem: A bakery packs 6 rolls in each bag. It has 38 rolls. How many more rolls does it need to fill the last bag?
questions.solution: $6 \times 6 = 36$, so 6 full bags use 36 rolls and 2 rolls are left. The last bag has 2 rolls and needs $6 - 2 = 4$ more.

solve.work: 38 = 6 x 6 + 2; last bag has 2, needs 6 - 2 = 4 more.

questions.skill: Remainders
questions.stem: A whole number between 40 and 49 leaves a remainder of 3 when it is divided by 7. What is the number?
questions.solution: Multiples of 7 near this range are 42 and 49. The number is 3 more than a multiple of 7: $42 + 3 = 45$. Check: $45 \div 7 = 6$ remainder 3.

questions.skill: Remainders
questions.stem: Which division has the greatest remainder?
questions.solution: $50 \div 9 = 5$ remainder 5, $50 \div 6 = 8$ remainder 2, $50 \div 7 = 7$ remainder 1, and $50 \div 8 = 6$ remainder 2. The greatest remainder is 5.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: multiply then subtract
questions.stem: Ben has 5 packs of cards with 8 cards in each pack. He gives 6 cards to a friend. How many cards does Ben have left?
questions.solution: First find how many cards Ben starts with: 5 x 8 = 40. Then subtract the 6 he gives away: 40 - 6 = 34.

questions.skill: Choose the equation that matches a story
questions.stem: Tom has 4 bags with the same number of marbles in each bag, and 3 loose marbles. He has 31 marbles in all. Let $n$ be the number of marbles in each bag. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: The 4 bags hold $4 \times n$ marbles. Adding the 3 loose marbles gives $4 \times n + 3$, and that equals 31. So the equation is $4 \times n + 3 = 31$.

solve.work: 4 bags of n marbles = 4 x n, plus 3 loose = 31: 4 x n + 3 = 31 (n = 7).

questions.skill: Two-step problem: divide then subtract
questions.stem: A farmer has 56 apples. He puts them into bags of 8 apples each. Then he sells 3 of the bags. How many bags are left?
questions.solution: 56 apples in bags of 8 makes 56 divided by 8 = 7 bags. After selling 3 bags, 7 - 3 = 4 bags are left.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: add and subtract
questions.stem: Lena had 25 stickers. She got 12 more from a friend, then gave 9 to her brother. How many stickers does Lena have now?
questions.solution: First add: $25 + 12 = 37$. Then subtract: $37 - 9 = 28$. The choice 37 stops after the first step, 46 adds all three numbers, and 22 swaps the adding and the subtracting.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: add and subtract
questions.stem: A bus has 30 riders. At the first stop 8 riders get off. At the second stop 5 riders get on. How many riders are on the bus now?
questions.solution: $30 - 8 = 22$ riders are left after the first stop. Then $22 + 5 = 27$ after the second stop.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: add and subtract
questions.stem: A school library had 250 books. It bought 40 new books and gave away 15 old books. How many books does the library have now?
questions.solution: After buying: $250 + 40 = 290$ books. After giving away: $290 - 15 = 275$ books.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: multiply, then add or subtract
questions.stem: A box has 6 rows of 4 crayons, and 3 more crayons are loose. How many crayons are there in all?
questions.solution: The rows hold $6 \times 4 = 24$ crayons. Add the loose ones: $24 + 3 = 27$ crayons.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: multiply, then add or subtract
questions.stem: Zoe buys 3 books that cost 5 dollars each. She also buys a bookmark for 2 dollars. How many dollars does she spend?
questions.solution: The books cost $3 \times 5 = 15$ dollars. Add the bookmark: $15 + 2 = 17$ dollars. The choice 10 adds all the numbers, 21 multiplies 3 by 7, and 30 multiplies all three.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: multiply, then add or subtract
questions.stem: Mr. Park buys 6 packs of pens. Each pack has 8 pens. He gives 15 pens to his class. How many pens does Mr. Park have left?
questions.solution: He buys $6 \times 8 = 48$ pens. After giving 15 away, $48 - 15 = 33$ pens are left. The choice 48 forgets to subtract, 63 adds instead, and 29 adds all three numbers.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: divide, then add or subtract
questions.stem: Sam has 20 cherries. He shares them equally among 4 friends. Then each friend gets 2 more cherries from Sam's mom. How many cherries does each friend have?
questions.solution: Sharing gives $20 \div 4 = 5$ cherries each. With 2 more, each friend has $5 + 2 = 7$ cherries.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: divide, then add or subtract
questions.stem: A teacher has 54 pencils packed in boxes of 6 pencils each. She then buys 4 more boxes. How many boxes does she have now?
questions.solution: The pencils fill $54 \div 6 = 9$ boxes. With 4 more boxes, she has $9 + 4 = 13$ boxes. The choice 9 stops after the first step, 58 adds 4 to the pencils, and 5 subtracts.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: divide, then add or subtract
questions.stem: A pack of 28 cards is split equally between 2 players. One player loses 3 cards. How many cards does that player have now?
questions.solution: Each player gets $28 \div 2 = 14$ cards. After losing 3, that player has $14 - 3 = 11$ cards.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: add or subtract, then multiply or divide
questions.stem: There are 8 girls and 7 boys in a club. Each member needs 2 pencils. How many pencils does the whole club need?
questions.solution: The club has $8 + 7 = 15$ members. They need $15 \times 2 = 30$ pencils. The choice 15 stops after the first step, and 22 only doubles the boys.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: add or subtract, then multiply or divide
questions.stem: Jo buys 5 tickets, and her sister buys 4 tickets. Each ticket costs 8 dollars. How many dollars do they spend in all?
questions.solution: They buy $5 + 4 = 9$ tickets. The cost is $9 \times 8 = 72$ dollars. The choice 40 counts only Jo's tickets.

questions.skill: Two-step problem: multiply and divide
