questions.solution: The two 9 cm sides use $9 + 9 = 18$ cm. That leaves $30 - 18 = 12$ cm for the other two sides, which are equal, so each is 6 cm. The three other sides are 9, 6 and 6 cm.

solve.work: Opposite sides equal: another side is 9; 30 - 18 = 12, so the other two are 6 and 6. Sides: 9, 6, 6.

questions.skill: Side lengths and perimeter of triangles and quadrilaterals
questions.stem: A square and an equilateral triangle have sides of the same length. The perimeter of the triangle is 18 cm. What is the perimeter of the square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Each side of the triangle is $18 \div 3 = 6$ cm. The square has sides of 6 cm too, so its perimeter is $4 \times 6 = 24$ cm.

questions.skill: Parallel sides and right angles of a quadrilateral
questions.stem: Here are six shapes: a square, a rectangle, a rhombus, a kite, a parallelogram and a triangle. Some of them have two pairs of parallel sides. Of those shapes, how many do NOT always have four right angles?
questions.solution: The shapes with two pairs of parallel sides are the square, the rectangle, the rhombus and the parallelogram. The kite and the triangle have none. A square and a rectangle always have four right angles. A rhombus and a parallelogram do not always have right angles. So 2 of them do not always have four right angles.

solve.work: Two pairs of parallel sides: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram (kite and triangle do not). Of these, rhombus and parallelogram need not have four right angles: 2.

questions.skill: Sort and count shapes by an attribute
questions.stem: A bag holds only triangles and quadrilaterals. There are 9 shapes in the bag, and together they have 31 sides. How many of the shapes are quadrilaterals?
questions.solution: A triangle has 3 sides and a quadrilateral has 4 sides. If all 9 shapes were triangles, there would be $9 \times 3 = 27$ sides. There are $31 - 27 = 4$ more sides, and each quadrilateral adds 1 extra side. So there are 4 quadrilaterals. Check: $5 \times 3 + 4 \times 4 = 15 + 16 = 31$.

solve.work: If all 9 were triangles: 27 sides. Each quadrilateral adds 1: 31-27=4 quadrilaterals (5 triangles: 15+16=31).

questions.skill: Side lengths and perimeter of triangles and quadrilaterals
questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has sides of 16 cm. A rhombus has the same perimeter as the triangle. How long is each side of the rhombus, in centimeters?
questions.solution: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides, so its perimeter is $3 \times 16 = 48$ centimeters. A rhombus has four equal sides, so each side is $48 \div 4 = 12$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Side lengths and perimeter of triangles and quadrilaterals
questions.stem: A rectangle is 11 cm long and 5 cm wide. A square has the same perimeter as the rectangle. How long is each side of the square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The perimeter of the rectangle is $11 + 5 + 11 + 5 = 32$ centimeters. A square has four equal sides, so each side is $32 \div 4 = 8$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Elapsed time in minutes
questions.stem: Sara starts her homework at 4:20 p.m. and finishes at 5:05 p.m. How many minutes does she work?
questions.solution: From 4:20 to 5:00 is 40 minutes. From 5:00 to 5:05 is 5 more minutes. 40 + 5 = 45 minutes.

questions.skill: Choose a unit for mass
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a pencil?
questions.solution: A pencil is very light, so use a small unit of mass: grams. A kilogram is 1,000 grams, much too big. Milliliters measure capacity and meters measure length.

solve.work: A pencil has a mass of a few grams.

questions.skill: Convert meters to centimeters
questions.stem: A rope is 3 meters long. How many centimeters long is it?
questions.solution: 1 meter is 100 centimeters, so 3 meters is 3 x 100 = 300 centimeters.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: Leo starts reading at 6:40 p.m. and stops at 7:10 p.m. How many minutes does he read?
questions.solution: From 6:40 to 7:00 is 20 minutes. From 7:00 to 7:10 is 10 more minutes. In all, $20 + 10 = 30$ minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: Practice starts at 3:15 p.m. and ends at 4:15 p.m. How much time passes?
questions.solution: From 3:15 to 4:15 the hour hand moves forward one hour and the minutes stay the same, so exactly 1 hour passes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: The first class of the day starts at 8:45 a.m. and ends at 9:35 a.m. How many minutes long is the class?
questions.solution: From 8:45 to 9:00 is 15 minutes. From 9:00 to 9:35 is 35 more minutes. In all, $15 + 35 = 50$ minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: A show starts at 1:00 p.m. and ends at 2:30 p.m. How long is the show?
questions.solution: From 1:00 to 2:00 is 1 hour, and from 2:00 to 2:30 is 30 more minutes. The show is 1 hour 30 minutes long.

solve.work: 1:00 to 2:00 is 1 hour, then 30 min more: 1 hour 30 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A lesson starts at 4:00 p.m. and lasts 30 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: Add 30 minutes to 4:00 p.m. to get 4:30 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A movie starts at 2:00 p.m. and lasts 2 hours. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: Add 2 hours to 2:00 p.m. to get 4:00 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A game starts at 2:10 p.m. and lasts 35 minutes. It ends before 3:00 p.m. How many minutes after 2:00 p.m. does it end?
questions.solution: Add 35 minutes to 2:10. The minutes go from 10 to $10 + 35 = 45$, which is still before 3:00, so the game ends at 2:45 p.m., which is 45 minutes after 2:00 p.m.

solve.work: 2:10 + 35 min = 2:45 p.m., which is 45 minutes after 2:00.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A lesson ends at 5:30 p.m. and lasts 30 minutes. At what time did it start?
questions.solution: Count back 30 minutes from 5:30 p.m. to get 5:00 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A walk ended at 4:50 p.m. and lasted 20 minutes. It started between 4:00 p.m. and 5:00 p.m. How many minutes after 4:00 p.m. did it start?
questions.solution: Count back 20 minutes from 4:50. The minutes go from 50 to $50 - 20 = 30$, so the walk started at 4:30 p.m., which is 30 minutes after 4:00 p.m.

questions.skill: Convert between hours and minutes
questions.stem: How many minutes are in 2 hours?
questions.solution: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour, so 2 hours is $2 \times 60 = 120$ minutes.

questions.skill: Convert between hours and minutes
questions.stem: A movie lasts 1 hour 40 minutes. How many minutes is that in all?
questions.solution: 1 hour is 60 minutes, so 1 hour 40 minutes is $60 + 40 = 100$ minutes.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
questions.solution: A pencil is a short length, so centimeters fit best. A kilometer is far too long, and a liter and a gram do not measure length.

solve.work: A pencil's length is a small length: centimeter. Gram and liter are not lengths; kilometer is far too big.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a bathtub holds?
questions.solution: A bathtub holds a lot of water, so liters fit best. A milliliter is a tiny amount, and a centimeter and a kilogram do not measure capacity.

solve.work: A bathtub holds a large amount of liquid: liter (milliliter too small).

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the distance between two towns?
questions.solution: The distance between towns is long, so kilometers fit best. A kilogram measures mass, not length.

solve.work: Distance between towns is long: kilometer.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a backpack full of books?
questions.solution: A full backpack is a few kilograms. A gram is too small, a liter measures capacity and a meter measures length.

solve.work: A full backpack is several kilograms: kilogram.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: A paper clip is about 3 centimeters long. About how many centimeters long is a row of 4 paper clips?
questions.solution: Four paper clips of 3 centimeters each make $4 \times 3 = 12$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A trail is 2 kilometers long. How many meters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer, so 2 kilometers is $2 \times 1{,}000 = 2{,}000$ meters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A beetle is 6 centimeters long. How many millimeters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 10 millimeters in 1 centimeter, so 6 centimeters is $6 \times 10 = 60$ millimeters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Which measure is equal to 1 kilometer?
questions.solution: "Kilo" means one thousand, so 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A bag of rice has a mass of 2 kilograms. How many grams is that?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 grams in 1 kilogram, so 2 kilograms is $2 \times 1{,}000 = 2{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Which mass is the same as 5 kilograms?
questions.solution: 1 kilogram is 1,000 grams, so 5 kilograms is $5 \times 1{,}000 = 5{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: One apple has a mass of 150 grams. What is the mass of 2 apples, in grams?
questions.solution: Two apples have a mass of $2 \times 150 = 300$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A bottle holds 2 liters of juice. How many milliliters is that?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter, so 2 liters is $2 \times 1{,}000 = 2{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A cup holds 250 milliliters. How many milliliters do 2 cups hold?
questions.solution: Two cups hold $2 \times 250 = 500$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Which unit is used to measure how much liquid a container holds?
questions.solution: Liters measure capacity, which is how much liquid a container holds. Grams measure mass, and meters and kilometers measure length.

solve.work: Liquid volume (capacity) is measured in liters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Ben says that 5 liters is 50 milliliters. How many milliliters is 5 liters?
questions.solution: 1 liter is 1,000 milliliters, so 5 liters is $5 \times 1{,}000 = 5{,}000$ milliliters. Ben multiplied by 10 instead of 1,000.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Which mass is the greatest?
questions.solution: 2 kilograms is 2,000 grams. That is more than 1,500 grams, 900 grams and 500 grams.

solve.work: 900 g, 2,000 g, 1,500 g, 500 g. Greatest: 2 kilograms.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Which pair of measures is equal?
questions.solution: 3 meters is $3 \times 100 = 300$ centimeters. In the other pairs, 3 kilometers is 3,000 meters, and 3 centimeters is 30 millimeters.

solve.work: 3 km = 3,000 m (no); 3 cm = 30 mm (no); 3 m = 300 cm (yes); 3 m is not 30 cm.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: A pencil is 19 centimeters long. A pen is 14 centimeters long. How many centimeters longer is the pencil?
questions.solution: Subtract the two lengths: $19 - 14 = 5$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A trail is 4 kilometers long. Which expression shows the length of the trail in meters?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer, so to change kilometers to meters, multiply by 1,000. The trail is $4 \times 1000 = 4{,}000$ meters long.

questions.skill: Capacity: convert and subtract
questions.stem: A jug holds 4 liters of water. Ben pours 750 milliliters into a glass. How many milliliters of water are left in the jug?
questions.solution: 4 liters is 4 x 1,000 = 4,000 milliliters. After pouring out 750 milliliters, 4,000 - 750 = 3,250 milliliters are left.

questions.skill: Elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: A bus leaves at 8:50 a.m. and arrives at 10:15 a.m. How long is the trip?
questions.solution: From 8:50 to 9:00 is 10 minutes. From 9:00 to 10:00 is 1 hour. From 10:00 to 10:15 is 15 minutes. Total: 1 hour and 10 + 15 = 25 minutes, so 1 hour 25 minutes.

questions.skill: Estimate a length
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
questions.solution: A door is a little taller than a tall adult, about 2 meters. 2 centimeters is about the width of a finger, and 20 meters or 2 kilometers are far too long.

solve.work: A door is about 2 m tall.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: A train leaves at 10:35 a.m. and arrives at 12:10 p.m. How many minutes long is the trip?
questions.solution: From 10:35 to 11:00 is 25 minutes. From 11:00 to 12:00 is 60 minutes. From 12:00 to 12:10 is 10 minutes. In all, $25 + 60 + 10 = 95$ minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: Nia starts her chores at 4:50 p.m. and finishes at 6:05 p.m. How long does she work?
questions.solution: From 4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes. From 5:00 to 6:00 is 1 hour. From 6:00 to 6:05 is 5 minutes. The total is 1 hour and $10 + 5 = 15$ minutes.

solve.work: 4:50 to 5:50 is 1 hour; 5:50 to 6:05 is 15 min: 1 hour 15 minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: A swim lesson goes from 3:40 p.m. to 4:20 p.m. How many minutes long is the lesson?
questions.solution: From 3:40 to 4:00 is 20 minutes, and from 4:00 to 4:20 is 20 more minutes. In all, $20 + 20 = 40$ minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: How much time passes from 11:20 a.m. to 12:05 p.m.?
questions.solution: From 11:20 to 12:00 is 40 minutes. From 12:00 to 12:05 is 5 more minutes. The total is $40 + 5 = 45$ minutes.

solve.work: 11:20 to 12:00 is 40 min; 12:00 to 12:05 is 5 min. 45 minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: A museum tour begins at 10:25 a.m. and ends at 11:50 a.m. How many minutes does the tour last?
questions.solution: From 10:25 to 11:00 is 35 minutes. From 11:00 to 11:50 is 50 more minutes. In all, $35 + 50 = 85$ minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A bus ride starts at 7:35 a.m. and takes 50 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: From 7:35 to 8:00 is 25 minutes. There are $50 - 25 = 25$ minutes left, so the ride ends at 8:25 a.m.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Soccer practice starts at 3:45 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes. It ends between 5:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. How many minutes after 5:00 p.m. does it end?
questions.solution: Add 1 hour to get 4:45 p.m. Then add 30 minutes: from 4:45 to 5:00 is 15 minutes, and 15 more minutes make 5:15 p.m. That is 15 minutes after 5:00 p.m.

solve.work: 3:45 + 1 hour = 4:45; + 30 min = 5:15 p.m. That is 15 minutes after 5:00.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A show starts at 11:40 a.m. and lasts 45 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: From 11:40 to 12:00 is 20 minutes. The show has $45 - 20 = 25$ minutes left, so it ends at 12:25 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A movie ended at 3:10 p.m. and lasted 1 hour 20 minutes. At what time did it start?
questions.solution: Count back 1 hour from 3:10 to get 2:10. Then count back 20 more minutes: 10 minutes to 2:00 and 10 more to 1:50. The movie started at 1:50 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: Dinner ended at 7:05 p.m. and lasted 50 minutes. It started between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. How many minutes after 6:00 p.m. did it start?
questions.solution: Count back 5 minutes to 7:00. There are $50 - 5 = 45$ minutes left to count back, and 45 minutes before 7:00 is 6:15, which is 15 minutes after 6:00 p.m.

questions.skill: Convert between hours and minutes
questions.stem: Which is the same length of time as 85 minutes?
questions.solution: 85 minutes is 60 minutes plus 25 minutes. That is 1 hour 25 minutes.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the length of a new pencil?
questions.solution: A new pencil fits in a hand and is a bit shorter than a ruler: about 19 centimeters. The other lengths are far too long.

solve.work: A new pencil is about 19 cm; 190 cm is taller than a child.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the mass of a loaf of bread?
questions.solution: A loaf of bread is about half a kilogram, or 500 grams. 5 grams is about a paper clip, and 5 or 500 kilograms is far too heavy.

solve.work: A loaf of bread is about half a kilogram: 500 grams.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the amount of juice in a small juice box?
questions.solution: A small juice box holds about a cup, which is about 200 milliliters. Liters are far too large, and 2 milliliters is only a few drops.

solve.work: A small juice box holds about 200 mL.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the height of a fourth-grade student?
questions.solution: A fourth grader is a little over 1 meter tall, about 135 centimeters. The other heights are far too tall or too short.

solve.work: A 9-10 year old is about 1.35 m tall: 135 centimeters.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: A cup holds about 250 milliliters. About how many cups of water fill a 1 liter jug?
questions.solution: 1 liter is 1,000 milliliters. Four cups of 250 milliliters make $4 \times 250 = 1{,}000$ milliliters, so about 4 cups fill the jug.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A path is 3 kilometers long. Ravi has walked 1,200 meters of it. How many meters are left?
questions.solution: 3 kilometers is 3,000 meters. The part left is $3{,}000 - 1{,}200 = 1{,}800$ meters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Tia jumped 2 meters 30 centimeters. How many centimeters is that?
questions.solution: 2 meters is 200 centimeters. Adding the 30 centimeters gives $200 + 30 = 230$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A bookshelf is 3 meters long. Each book is 5 centimeters thick. How many books fit side by side along the whole shelf?
questions.solution: 3 meters is 300 centimeters. The number of books is $300 \div 5 = 60$.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Which length is equal to 3 meters 7 centimeters?
questions.solution: 3 meters is 300 centimeters. Adding 7 centimeters gives 307 centimeters. The 7 goes in the ones place, so there is a 0 in the tens place.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A puppy has a mass of 4 kilograms 250 grams. How many grams is that?
questions.solution: 4 kilograms is 4,000 grams. Adding 250 grams gives $4{,}000 + 250 = 4{,}250$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Five bags of rice have a mass of 2 kilograms each. What is the total mass of the bags, in grams?
questions.solution: The bags have $5 \times 2 = 10$ kilograms in all. That is $10 \times 1{,}000 = 10{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Which mass is NOT equal to 2 kilograms?
questions.solution: 2 kilograms is 2,000 grams. 1,000 + 1,000 is 2,000 grams and 1 kilogram plus 1,000 grams is also 2,000 grams. But 200 grams is only a tenth as much.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A cake recipe uses 1 kilogram 200 grams of flour and 450 grams of sugar. What is the total mass of the flour and sugar, in grams?
questions.solution: 1 kilogram 200 grams is 1,200 grams. Adding the sugar gives $1{,}200 + 450 = 1{,}650$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A fish tank needs 5 liters of water. Dev has poured in 3,200 milliliters so far. How many more milliliters does he need?
questions.solution: 5 liters is 5,000 milliliters. He still needs $5{,}000 - 3{,}200 = 1{,}800$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A bottle holds 3 liters 400 milliliters. Which shows that amount in milliliters?
questions.solution: 3 liters is 3,000 milliliters. Adding 400 milliliters gives $3{,}000 + 400 = 3{,}400$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A large bottle holds 2 liters. A small bottle holds 500 milliliters. How many small bottles hold the same amount as the large bottle?
questions.solution: 2 liters is 2,000 milliliters. The number of small bottles is $2{,}000 \div 500 = 4$.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Which length is the longest?
questions.solution: Change each to centimeters. 3 meters is 300. 290 stays 290. 2 meters 95 centimeters is 295. And 305 is the greatest.

solve.work: 305 cm; 300 cm; 295 cm; 290 cm. Longest: 305 centimeters.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Which comparison is correct?
questions.solution: 4 liters is 4,000 milliliters, which is more than 3,900 milliliters.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Sara has a ribbon that is 2 meters long. Tom has a ribbon that is 175 centimeters long. How many centimeters longer is Sara's ribbon?
questions.solution: 2 meters is 200 centimeters. Sara's ribbon is $200 - 175 = 25$ centimeters longer.

questions.skill: Mass: convert and subtract
questions.stem: A recipe needs 2 kilograms of flour. Mia has 1,450 grams of flour. How many more grams of flour does she need?
questions.solution: 2 kilograms is 2 x 1,000 = 2,000 grams. She needs 2,000 - 1,450 = 550 more grams.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Practice starts at 3:35 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: Add 1 hour: 3:35 + 1 hour = 4:35. Add 50 minutes: 4:35 to 5:00 is 25 minutes, and 25 more minutes make 50, so the end time is 5:25 p.m.

questions.skill: Capacity: convert then divide
questions.stem: A water bottle holds 500 milliliters. How many bottles can be filled completely from 6 liters of water?
questions.solution: 6 liters is 6 x 1,000 = 6,000 milliliters. Each bottle takes 500 milliliters, so 6,000 divided by 500 = 12 bottles.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: A baseball game starts at 6:45 p.m. and ends at 9:20 p.m. How many minutes long is the game?
questions.solution: From 6:45 to 7:00 is 15 minutes. From 7:00 to 9:00 is 2 hours, which is 120 minutes. From 9:00 to 9:20 is 20 minutes. In all, $15 + 120 + 20 = 155$ minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: Four trips are listed. A: 7:45 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. B: 9:10 a.m. to 10:05 a.m. C: 11:50 a.m. to 12:40 p.m. D: 1:25 p.m. to 2:10 p.m. Which trip takes the most time?
questions.solution: Trip A takes 45 minutes, trip B takes 55 minutes, trip C takes 50 minutes and trip D takes 45 minutes. Trip B takes the most time.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: A flight leaves at 11:35 a.m. and lands at 2:25 p.m. on the same day. How long is the flight?
questions.solution: From 11:35 a.m. to 2:35 p.m. would be exactly 3 hours. The flight lands 10 minutes before that, so it takes 2 hours 50 minutes. Another way: 25 minutes to 12:00, 2 hours to 2:00, and 25 minutes to 2:25, which is 170 minutes.

solve.work: 11:35 a.m. to 2:35 p.m. is 3 hours; 2:25 is 10 min earlier: 2 hours 50 minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time across the hour
questions.stem: Mia has two lessons. The first goes from 3:20 p.m. to 4:05 p.m. The second goes from 4:15 p.m. to 5:40 p.m. How many minutes long are the two lessons added together?
questions.solution: The first lesson lasts 40 + 5 = 45 minutes (3:20 to 4:00, then 4:00 to 4:05). The second lasts 45 + 40 = 85 minutes (4:15 to 5:00, then 5:00 to 5:40). Together, $45 + 85 = 130$ minutes. The break between the lessons does not count.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A cooking class starts at 5:50 p.m. and lasts 2 hours 25 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: Add 2 hours to get 7:50 p.m. From 7:50 to 8:00 is 10 minutes, and the other 15 minutes take it to 8:15 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A rehearsal starts at 2:50 p.m. and lasts 85 minutes. It ends between 4:00 p.m. and 5:00 p.m. How many minutes after 4:00 p.m. does it end?
questions.solution: 85 minutes is 1 hour 25 minutes. One hour after 2:50 is 3:50. From 3:50 to 4:00 is 10 minutes, and the other 15 minutes make 4:15 p.m. That is 15 minutes after 4:00 p.m.

solve.work: 85 min = 1 h 25 min. 2:50 + 1 h = 3:50; + 25 min = 4:15 p.m. 15 minutes after 4:00.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A concert ended at 10:15 p.m. and lasted 2 hours 40 minutes. At what time did it start?
questions.solution: Count back 2 hours from 10:15 to get 8:15. Then count back 40 minutes: 15 minutes to 8:00 and 25 more to 7:35. The concert started at 7:35 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A class ended at 2:05 p.m. and lasted 95 minutes. It started between 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 p.m. How many minutes after 12:00 p.m. did it start?
questions.solution: 95 minutes is 1 hour 35 minutes. One hour before 2:05 is 1:05. Then 35 minutes before 1:05 is 12:30: 5 minutes to 1:00 and 30 more to 12:30. That is 30 minutes after 12:00 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A hike ended at 12:20 p.m. after lasting 3 hours 45 minutes. At what time did it start?
questions.solution: Count back 3 hours from 12:20 p.m. to get 9:20 a.m. Then count back 45 minutes: 20 minutes to 9:00 and 25 more to 8:35. The hike started at 8:35 a.m.

questions.skill: Convert between hours and minutes
questions.stem: A road trip takes 3 hours 25 minutes. How many minutes is that in all?
questions.solution: 3 hours is $3 \times 60 = 180$ minutes. Adding the 25 minutes gives $180 + 25 = 205$ minutes.

questions.skill: Convert between hours and minutes
questions.stem: Which amount of time is the longest?
questions.solution: Change each to minutes. 2 hours is 120 minutes. 110 minutes stays 110. 1 hour 55 minutes is $60 + 55 = 115$ minutes. The longest is 125 minutes.

solve.work: 110; 125; 1 h 55 min = 115; 2 h = 120. Longest is 125 minutes.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the mass of a pet cat?
questions.solution: A pet cat has a mass of a few kilograms. 4 grams is about a paper clip, and 40 or 400 kilograms is far too heavy.

solve.work: A pet cat is about 4 kg; 40 kg is a large dog.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the amount of water in a full bucket?
questions.solution: A bucket holds several liters, so 10 liters is reasonable. 10 or 100 milliliters is only a few spoonfuls, and 1,000 liters is as much as a large tank.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: A paper clip has a mass of about 1 gram. About how many paper clips have a total mass of 1 kilogram?
questions.solution: 1 kilogram is 1,000 grams. Each clip is about 1 gram, so about $1{,}000 \div 1 = 1{,}000$ paper clips.

questions.skill: Estimate and choose a metric unit
questions.stem: Ravi says that a school bus is about 12 centimeters long. Which unit should he use instead to give a sensible length?
questions.solution: A bus is longer than a classroom, so about 12 meters. 12 centimeters is about the length of a pencil. Millimeters are even smaller, kilometers are far too long, and kilograms measure mass, not length.

solve.work: A school bus is about 12 meters long.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A trail is 4 kilometers long. A hiker walks the whole trail 3 times. How many meters does the hiker walk in all?
questions.solution: 4 kilometers is 4,000 meters. Three trips make $3 \times 4{,}000 = 12{,}000$ meters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Three ribbons are 1 meter 20 centimeters, 85 centimeters and 2 meters long. What is their total length?
questions.solution: Change each to centimeters: 1 meter 20 centimeters is 120 centimeters, 85 centimeters stays 85, and 2 meters is 200 centimeters. The total is $120 + 85 + 200 = 405$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A rod is 3 meters long. Pieces that are each 25 centimeters long are cut from it. How many pieces can be cut from the whole rod?
questions.solution: 3 meters is 300 centimeters. The number of pieces is $300 \div 25 = 12$.

questions.skill: Metric length: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Sam says that 7 meters is 70 centimeters. What mistake did he make?
choices: He multiplied by 1,000 instead of by 100.
He multiplied by 10 instead of by 100.
He divided by 100 instead of multiplying.
questions.answer: He multiplied by 10 instead of by 100.
questions.solution: 7 meters is $7 \times 100 = 700$ centimeters. Sam got 70, which is $7 \times 10$, so he used 10 instead of 100.

solve.answer: He multiplied by 10 instead of by 100.
solve.work: 7 m = 700 cm. 7 x 10 = 70, so he multiplied by 10 instead of 100.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Pam buys 3 bags of apples that are 2 kilograms each and a melon with a mass of 750 grams. What is the total mass of her fruit, in grams?
questions.solution: The apples have $3 \times 2 = 6$ kilograms, which is 6,000 grams. Adding the melon gives $6{,}000 + 750 = 6{,}750$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A shipment has 5 boxes. Each box has a mass of 1 kilogram 300 grams. What is the total mass of the shipment, in grams?
questions.solution: Each box is 1,300 grams. Five boxes have a mass of $5 \times 1{,}300 = 6{,}500$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Max has a 2 kilogram bag of flour. He uses 125 grams of flour for each loaf, and he bakes 8 loaves. How many grams of flour are left?
questions.solution: 2 kilograms is 2,000 grams. The loaves use $8 \times 125 = 1{,}000$ grams. That leaves $2{,}000 - 1{,}000 = 1{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A 2 liter bottle of juice is on the table. Four friends each drink 350 milliliters from it. How many milliliters of juice are left?
questions.solution: 2 liters is 2,000 milliliters. The friends drink $4 \times 350 = 1{,}400$ milliliters. What is left is $2{,}000 - 1{,}400 = 600$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A tap fills 3 liters of water each minute. How many milliliters of water flow from the tap in 5 minutes?
questions.solution: In 5 minutes the tap fills $3 \times 5 = 15$ liters. That is $15 \times 1{,}000 = 15{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A jug holds 5 liters. Eight glasses of 300 milliliters each are poured from it. How much water is left in the jug?
questions.solution: 5 liters is 5,000 milliliters. The glasses use $8 \times 300 = 2{,}400$ milliliters. What is left is $5{,}000 - 2{,}400 = 2{,}600$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Metric capacity: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: A bottle holds 1 liter 500 milliliters. How many milliliters do 4 of these bottles hold in all?
questions.solution: One bottle holds 1,500 milliliters. Four bottles hold $4 \times 1{,}500 = 6{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Four masses are A: 2 kilograms, B: 1,800 grams, C: 2 kilograms 100 grams, and D: 1 kilogram 950 grams. Which list puts them in order from lightest to heaviest?
questions.solution: In grams, A is 2,000, B is 1,800, C is 2,100 and D is 1,950. From lightest to heaviest: B (1,800), D (1,950), A (2,000), C (2,100).

solve.work: A 2,000 g; B 1,800 g; C 2,100 g; D 1,950 g. Lightest to heaviest: B, D, A, C.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Tank A holds 4 liters 200 milliliters of water. Tank B holds 3,750 milliliters. How many milliliters more does tank A hold than tank B?
questions.solution: Tank A holds $4{,}000 + 200 = 4{,}200$ milliliters. The difference is $4{,}200 - 3{,}750 = 450$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Compare and order metric measurements
questions.stem: Rope A is 3 meters 20 centimeters long. Rope B is 340 centimeters long. Rope C is 3 meters 5 centimeters long. How many centimeters long is the shortest rope?
questions.solution: In centimeters, rope A is 320, rope B is 340 and rope C is $300 + 5 = 305$. The shortest is rope C at 305 centimeters.

solve.work: A = 320 cm, B = 340 cm, C = 305 cm. Shortest is 305.

questions.skill: Metric mass: convert larger units to smaller and solve
questions.stem: Six identical bags of rice have a total mass of 3 kilograms 300 grams. What is the mass of one bag, in grams?
questions.solution: 3 kilograms 300 grams is $3 \times 1000 + 300 = 3300$ grams. Six bags share this equally, so one bag has a mass of $3300 \div 6 = 550$ grams.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = length x width = 8 x 5 = 40 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle
questions.stem: What is the perimeter, in centimeters, of a rectangle that is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide?
questions.solution: Perimeter = 2 x (length + width) = 2 x (9 + 4) = 2 x 13 = 26 centimeters. (36 is the area, 13 is only half of the way around and 22 leaves out one of the widths.)

questions.skill: Choose the perimeter formula
questions.stem: Which expression gives the perimeter of a rectangle that is 12 m long and 5 m wide?
questions.solution: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so the perimeter is $2 \times (12 + 5)$. $12 \times 5$ is the area.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: A rug is 6 feet long and 3 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
questions.solution: Area = length $\times$ width = $6 \times 3 = 18$ square feet.

solve.work: Area = length x width = 6 x 3 = 18 square feet.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: A poster is 5 feet tall and 4 feet wide. What is the area of the poster in square feet?
questions.solution: Area = $5 \times 4 = 20$ square feet. Adding the sides gives 9, and 18 is the perimeter.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: Mia covers the top of a box with paper. The top is 8 inches long and 6 inches wide. How many square inches of paper does she need to cover it exactly?
questions.solution: The top is a rectangle, so the paper needed is its area: $8 \times 6 = 48$ square inches.

solve.work: Area of top = 8 x 6 = 48 square inches.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: A swimming pool is 12 meters long and 5 meters wide. What is the area of the water's surface in square meters?
questions.solution: Area = $12 \times 5 = 60$ square meters. Adding gives 17, the perimeter is 34, and subtracting gives 7.

solve.work: Surface area = 12 x 5 = 60 square meters. Distractors 34 (perimeter), 17 (sum), 7 (difference).

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: A rectangular table is 7 feet long and 3 feet wide. How many square feet is the area of its top?
questions.solution: $7 \times 3 = 21$ square feet.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: A picture frame is a rectangle 8 inches long and 6 inches wide. What is the perimeter of the frame in inches?
questions.solution: Perimeter = $2 \times (8 + 6) = 28$ inches. 14 adds only two sides, 48 is the area, and 20 leaves out one side.

solve.work: Perimeter = 2 x (8 + 6) = 28 inches. 14 is half, 48 the area.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: Sam walks once around the edge of a rectangular playground that is 20 meters long and 10 meters wide. How many meters does he walk?
questions.solution: He walks the perimeter: $2 \times (20 + 10) = 60$ meters. 30 is half the way around and 200 is the area.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: A rectangular garden bed is 5 feet long and 3 feet wide. How many feet of edging are needed to go all the way around it?
questions.solution: The edging goes around the perimeter: $5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16$ feet.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle in context
questions.stem: A rectangular bookmark is 11 centimeters long and 2 centimeters wide. A ribbon is glued along its whole edge. How many centimeters of ribbon are glued on?
questions.solution: Perimeter = $2 \times (11 + 2) = 26$ centimeters. 13 is only half the way around, 22 is the area, and 24 leaves out one short side.

solve.work: Perimeter = 2 x (11 + 2) = 26 cm. 22 is the area, 13 half the perimeter.

questions.skill: Find a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 30 square inches and a length of 5 inches. What is its width in inches?
questions.solution: Area = length $\times$ width, so width = $30 \div 5 = 6$ inches. Subtracting gives 25, adding gives 35, and multiplying gives 150.

questions.skill: Find a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rug covers 18 square feet of floor and is 6 feet long. How wide is the rug, in feet?
questions.solution: Width = area $\div$ length = $18 \div 6 = 3$ feet.

questions.skill: Find a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangular window pane has an area of 56 square inches. It is 8 inches tall. How many inches wide is it?
questions.solution: Width = area $\div$ height = $56 \div 8 = 7$ inches.

questions.skill: Find a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 45 square units and a length of 9 units. Which equation can be used to find the width, $w$?
questions.solution: Length $\times$ width = area, so $9 \times w = 45$ and $w = 5$.

solve.work: Area = length x width, so 9 x w = 45 (w = 5). Other options use the wrong operation.

questions.skill: Find a missing side from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangular banner needs 24 feet of trim all the way around its edge. The banner is 8 feet long. How many feet wide is it?
questions.solution: The two lengths use $8 + 8 = 16$ feet, leaving $24 - 16 = 8$ feet for the two widths. One width is $8 \div 2 = 4$ feet.

solve.work: Perimeter 24, so length + width = 12. Width = 12 - 8 = 4 feet.

questions.skill: Find a missing side from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 18 meters and a width of 3 meters. What is its length in meters?
questions.solution: The two widths use 6 meters, leaving $18 - 6 = 12$ meters for the two lengths, so one length is 6 meters. 9 is half the perimeter, which is length plus width.

questions.skill: Find a missing side from the perimeter
questions.stem: The two lengths of a rectangle add up to 10 cm, and its perimeter is 16 cm. How many centimeters is one width?
questions.solution: The two widths use $16 - 10 = 6$ cm, so one width is $6 \div 2 = 3$ cm.

solve.work: Perimeter = two lengths + two widths. Two widths = 16 - 10 = 6 cm, so one width = 3 cm.

questions.skill: Area of a rectilinear figure: add rectangles
questions.stem: An L-shaped patio is made of a 6 foot by 3 foot rectangle joined to a 4 foot by 2 foot rectangle. The two parts touch along an edge but do not overlap. What is the area of the patio in square feet?
questions.solution: $6 \times 3 = 18$ and $4 \times 2 = 8$. Total area = $18 + 8 = 26$ square feet.

questions.skill: Area of a rectilinear figure: add rectangles
questions.stem: A figure is made of a 3 by 4 rectangle and a 2 by 5 rectangle that do not overlap. What is the total area of the figure in square units?
questions.solution: $3 \times 4 = 12$ and $2 \times 5 = 10$, and $12 + 10 = 22$ square units. 12 counts only one part, 14 adds the sides, and 45 treats the figure as one big rectangle.

questions.skill: Area of a rectilinear figure: add rectangles
questions.stem: Two square stickers are placed side by side so they touch along one edge. One has sides of 3 inches and the other has sides of 2 inches. What is the total area they cover, in square inches?
questions.solution: $3 \times 3 = 9$ and $2 \times 2 = 4$. Together they cover $9 + 4 = 13$ square inches.

solve.work: 3 x 3 + 2 x 2 = 9 + 4 = 13 square inches (no overlap since they only touch along an edge).
