questions.skill: Fixed area, changing perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 60 square inches and sides that are whole numbers of inches. What is the smallest perimeter it could have, in inches?
questions.solution: Pairs: 1 by 60, 2 by 30, 3 by 20, 4 by 15, 5 by 12, 6 by 10. The pair closest in size, 6 by 10, has the smallest perimeter: $2 \times (6 + 10) = 32$ inches.

questions.skill: Fixed area, changing perimeter
questions.stem: Two rectangular pens each have an area of 48 square meters. Pen A is 8 meters wide. Pen B is 3 meters wide. How many more meters of fence does pen B need than pen A?
questions.solution: Pen A is $48 \div 8 = 6$ m long, so its fence is $2 \times (8 + 6) = 28$ m. Pen B is $48 \div 3 = 16$ m long, so its fence is $2 \times (3 + 16) = 38$ m. Pen B needs $38 - 28 = 10$ more meters.

solve.work: Pen A: 8 x 6, perimeter 28. Pen B: 3 x 16, perimeter 38. B needs 38 - 28 = 10 more meters.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter, changing area
questions.stem: Two rectangles each have a perimeter of 46 units. Rectangle R is 17 units long and rectangle S is 12 units long. How many square units greater is the area of S than the area of R?
questions.solution: Length plus width is $46 \div 2 = 23$. R is 6 wide: $17 \times 6 = 102$. S is 11 wide: $12 \times 11 = 132$. The difference is $132 - 102 = 30$ square units.

solve.work: Length + width = 23. R: 17 x 6 = 102. S: 12 x 11 = 132. Difference = 132 - 102 = 30 square units.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter, changing area
questions.stem: A farmer has 60 meters of fence and uses all of it for each pen. Pen 1 is rectangular and 20 meters long. Pen 2 is rectangular and 15 meters long. How many square meters greater is the area of the larger pen than the area of the smaller pen?
questions.solution: Length plus width is $60 \div 2 = 30$. Pen 1 is 10 wide: $20 \times 10 = 200$. Pen 2 is 15 wide: $15 \times 15 = 225$. The difference is $225 - 200 = 25$ square meters.

solve.work: Length + width = 30. Pen 1: 20 x 10 = 200. Pen 2: 15 x 15 = 225. Difference = 25 square meters.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter, changing area
questions.stem: A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The rectangle is 14 units long and 6 units wide. How many more square units of area does the square have than the rectangle?
questions.solution: The rectangle's perimeter is $2 \times (14 + 6) = 40$, so the square's sides are $40 \div 4 = 10$. Square: $10 \times 10 = 100$. Rectangle: $14 \times 6 = 84$. Difference: 16 square units.

solve.work: Rectangle perimeter = 2 x (14 + 6) = 40, area 84. Square side = 40 / 4 = 10, area 100. Difference = 16 square units.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter, changing area
questions.stem: A rectangle is 12 units long and 4 units wide. Its length is made 2 units shorter and its width is made 2 units longer. Which statement is true?
choices: The perimeter stays the same; the area decreases by 12 square units
The perimeter stays the same; the area increases by 12 square units
The perimeter stays the same; the area stays the same
The perimeter decreases; the area increases by 12 square units
questions.answer: The perimeter stays the same; the area increases by 12 square units
questions.solution: Old: 12 by 4, perimeter 32, area 48. New: 10 by 6, perimeter 32, area 60. The perimeter is the same and the area goes up by $60 - 48 = 12$ square units.

solve.answer: The perimeter stays the same; the area increases by 12 square units
solve.work: Original 12 x 4: perimeter 32, area 48. New 10 x 6: perimeter 32, area 60. Perimeter same, area up 12.

questions.skill: Choose area or perimeter for the situation
questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 15 meters long and 9 meters wide. Marta puts a fence around it and also spreads mulch over the whole garden. The fence costs 5 dollars per meter and the mulch costs 2 dollars per square meter. How many dollars do the fence and the mulch cost together?
questions.solution: Fence: the perimeter is $2 \times (15 + 9) = 48$ meters, which costs $48 \times 5 = 240$ dollars. Mulch: the area is $15 \times 9 = 135$ square meters, which costs $135 \times 2 = 270$ dollars. Together: $240 + 270 = 510$ dollars.

solve.work: Perimeter = 2 x (15 + 9) = 48 m; fence = 48 x 5 = 240. Area = 15 x 9 = 135; mulch = 135 x 2 = 270. Total = 510 dollars.

questions.skill: Choose area or perimeter for the situation
questions.stem: Yard A is 30 feet by 10 feet. Yard B is 20 feet by 20 feet. Which statement is true?
choices: They need the same amount of fence, but yard B has the greater area
Yard A needs more fence, and yard B has the greater area
They need the same amount of fence and have the same area
Yard B needs more fence and has the greater area
questions.answer: They need the same amount of fence, but yard B has the greater area
questions.solution: Both perimeters are 80 feet. Yard A has area $30 \times 10 = 300$ and yard B has area $20 \times 20 = 400$ square feet.

solve.answer: They need the same amount of fence, but yard B has the greater area
solve.work: A: perimeter 2 x 40 = 80, area 300. B: perimeter 2 x 40 = 80, area 400. Same fence, B greater area.

questions.skill: Square area and perimeter
questions.stem: A square garden has an area of 144 square feet. What is the perimeter of the garden in feet?
questions.solution: Since $12 \times 12 = 144$, each side is 12 feet. Perimeter = $4 \times 12 = 48$ feet.

solve.work: Side x side = 144, side = 12 ft. Perimeter = 4 x 12 = 48 feet.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectilinear figure
questions.stem: An L-shaped piece of cardboard is a 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle with a 5 cm by 3 cm rectangle cut out of one corner. What is the perimeter of the L-shaped piece, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Cutting a rectangle out of a corner moves the edge inward but does not change its total length. The perimeter is the same as the whole rectangle's: $2 \times (12 + 8) = 40$ cm.

solve.work: Cutting a rectangle from a corner replaces two edge pieces with two equal inner edges, so the perimeter equals the original rectangle's: 2 x (12 + 8) = 40 cm. E.g. 5 cut along the 12 side, 3 along the 8 side: sides 12, 8, 7, 3, 5, 5, sum 40. Either orientation fits (5 < 8, 3 < 12).

questions.skill: Same perimeter, different area
questions.stem: Rectangle P is 7 units long and 5 units wide. Rectangle Q has the same perimeter as rectangle P, and Q is 9 units long. How many more square units of area does rectangle P have than rectangle Q?
questions.solution: The perimeter of P is 2 x (7 + 5) = 24 units, so a length and a width of Q add up to 24 / 2 = 12. Q is 9 units long, so it is 12 - 9 = 3 units wide. The area of P is 7 x 5 = 35 square units. The area of Q is 9 x 3 = 27 square units. P has 35 - 27 = 8 more square units.

solve.work: Perimeter of P = 2 x (7 + 5) = 24. Q has perimeter 24 and length 9, so 9 + width = 12, width = 3. Area P = 7 x 5 = 35; area Q = 9 x 3 = 27. Difference = 35 - 27 = 8.

questions.skill: Range of a data set
questions.stem: Five students read 3, 5, 5, 8 and 9 books. What is the range of the number of books?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value: 9 - 3 = 6.

questions.skill: Mode of a data set
questions.stem: What is the mode of these numbers: 4, 7, 7, 2, 9, 7, 4?
questions.solution: The mode is the value that appears most often. 7 appears 3 times, 4 appears 2 times, and 2 and 9 appear once. The mode is 7.

solve.work: 7 appears 3 times, 4 twice, others once. Mode 7.

questions.skill: Numerical versus categorical questions
questions.stem: Which question can be answered with a number, so it is a numerical question?
choices: Which sport do you like best?
How many pets do you have?
questions.answer: How many pets do you have?
questions.solution: A numerical question is answered with a number. "How many pets do you have?" is answered with a number. The others are answered with a color, a sport or a food, which are categories.

solve.answer: How many pets do you have?
solve.work: Pets is answered with a count; the others with a category.

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Which of these is a categorical question, one whose answers are words or names rather than numbers?
choices: How many pencils are in your bag?
How tall are you in inches?
How many minutes did you read last night?
questions.solution: Answers like red, blue or green are words, so the question is categorical. The other three are answered with numbers.

solve.work: Favorite color is answered with a word (red, blue). The other three are answered with numbers (minutes, pencils, inches).

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Ava asks her classmates, "How many brothers and sisters do you have?" What kind of question is it?
choices: Numerical, because every answer is a word
Numerical, because every answer is a number
Categorical, because every answer is a number
Categorical, because many students will answer it
questions.answer: Numerical, because every answer is a number
questions.solution: Answers such as 0, 1, 2 and 3 are numbers, so the question is numerical.

solve.answer: Numerical, because every answer is a number
solve.work: Number of brothers and sisters is answered with a number (0, 1, 2...), so it is numerical; the reason is that every answer is a number.

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Four survey questions are listed. 1. What is your favorite snack? 2. How many cousins do you have? 3. What color is your backpack? 4. In which month is your birthday? Which question number is the only numerical question?
questions.solution: Only question 2 is answered with a number. The others are answered with names (snacks, colors, months), so they are categorical.

solve.work: 1 snack: word. 2 cousins: number. 3 backpack color: word. 4 birthday month: a month name. Only question 2 is numerical.

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Sam asked his friends a question and wrote down the answers: 3, 0, 1, 2, 1. Which question did he most likely ask?
choices: What kind of pet do you have?
How many pets do you have?
questions.answer: How many pets do you have?
questions.solution: The answers are numbers, so the question must be one answered with a number: how many pets.

solve.answer: How many pets do you have?
solve.work: Answers 3, 0, 1, 2, 1 are counts, so the question asks how many. Only 'How many pets do you have?' gives numbers.

questions.skill: Plan how to collect data
questions.stem: Ria wants to find out which lunch the students in her grade like best. Which is the best way to collect the data?
choices: Ask only her two best friends what they like
Ask only the students who sit at her lunch table
Pick the lunch she likes best and call that the answer
Ask students in every class to pick their favorite from a list of lunches
questions.answer: Ask students in every class to pick their favorite from a list of lunches
questions.solution: Asking students from every class gives data from the whole grade. The other plans leave out most of the students.

solve.answer: Ask students in every class to pick their favorite from a list of lunches
solve.work: To represent the whole grade, ask students in every class to choose from the same list. The other options use tiny or biased samples or no data.

questions.skill: Choose a graph or a scale
questions.stem: Nora recorded how many pages each of 12 students read last night. She wants a graph that puts an X above a number line for each student. Which graph should she make?
questions.solution: A line plot uses a number line with an X for each piece of data.

solve.work: An X above a number line for each data value is a line plot.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: A frequency table shows how many students chose each pet. Dog: 7 students. Cat: 5 students. Fish: 3 students. How many students chose a dog or a cat?
questions.solution: $7 + 5 = 12$ students.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: A tally chart for favorite colors shows 3 full groups of five tally marks and 2 more tally marks for the color blue. How many students chose blue?
questions.solution: Each full group is 5, so $3 \times 5 = 15$. Adding the 2 extra marks gives $15 + 2 = 17$ students.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: In a frequency table, what does the frequency of a value tell you?
choices: How many times the value appears in the data
The difference between the greatest and least values
Which value is in the middle
questions.answer: How many times the value appears in the data
questions.solution: Frequency means how often: the number of times a value appears.

solve.answer: How many times the value appears in the data
solve.work: Frequency is the number of times a value appears in the data.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: A list of data is 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4. Which frequency table matches the list?
questions.solution: In the list, 2 appears once, 3 appears twice and 4 appears three times.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: In a vote for a class pet, the hamster got 11 votes and the rabbit got 7 votes. How many more votes did the hamster get?
questions.solution: $11 - 7 = 4$ more votes.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: Students voted for a field trip. Zoo: 12 votes. Museum: 9 votes. Park: 15 votes. Aquarium: 6 votes. Which trip got the fewest votes?
questions.solution: The aquarium has the smallest number, 6.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: In a survey of 20 students, 8 chose soccer, 7 chose swimming, and the rest chose tennis. How many students chose tennis?
questions.solution: Soccer and swimming are $8 + 7 = 15$ students. The rest are $20 - 15 = 5$ students.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of pets owned by students. There are 4 Xs above 0, 6 Xs above 1 and 5 Xs above 2. How many students are shown on the line plot?
questions.solution: Each X is one student: $4 + 6 + 5 = 15$ students.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of books students read. There is 1 X above 1, 3 Xs above 2, 5 Xs above 3 and 2 Xs above 4. Above which number is the tallest stack of Xs?
questions.solution: The tallest stack is the one with the most Xs, which is 5 Xs above the number 3.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: The numbers of letters in the first names of 8 students are 4, 5, 3, 5, 6, 4, 5 and 3. If the data were put on a line plot, how many Xs would be above 5?
questions.solution: Each value of 5 gets one X. The list has three 5s, so there would be 3 Xs above 5.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the goals a team scored in its games. There is 1 X above 0, 3 Xs above 1, 5 Xs above 2, 4 Xs above 3 and 2 Xs above 4. In how many games did the team score fewer than 3 goals?
questions.solution: Fewer than 3 goals means 0, 1 or 2 goals: $1 + 3 + 5 = 9$ games.

questions.skill: Read a bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph shows how many students chose each snack. The bar for apples reaches 12, the bar for crackers reaches 9 and the bar for popcorn reaches 15. How many more students chose popcorn than crackers?
questions.solution: $15 - 9 = 6$ more students. (3 is popcorn minus apples, 24 is popcorn plus crackers, and 21 is apples plus crackers.)

questions.skill: Read a bar graph
questions.stem: The scale of a bar graph counts by 2s: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. A bar reaches the fourth line above 0. What number does the bar show?
questions.solution: The lines above 0 are 2, 4, 6 and 8, so the fourth line is $4 \times 2 = 8$.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph compares two classes. For pizza, the bar for Room 4 reaches 9 and the bar for Room 5 reaches 6. How many more students in Room 4 than in Room 5 chose pizza?
questions.solution: $9 - 6 = 3$ more students.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph shows how many boys and how many girls chose each sport. For soccer, the boys' bar reaches 8 and the girls' bar reaches 11. Which statement is true?
choices: More boys than girls chose soccer
More girls than boys chose soccer
The same number of boys and girls chose soccer
questions.answer: More girls than boys chose soccer
questions.solution: The girls' bar (11) is taller than the boys' bar (8), so more girls chose soccer.

solve.answer: More girls than boys chose soccer
solve.work: Girls 11 > boys 8, so more girls than boys chose soccer. Total is 19, not 8.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph has two bars side by side for each category. What is it mainly used for?
choices: Showing the order in which events happened
Showing each value as an X above a number line
Finding the middle number of a data set
Comparing two sets of data across the same categories
questions.answer: Comparing two sets of data across the same categories
questions.solution: The two bars in each category let you compare two groups, such as boys and girls.

solve.answer: Comparing two sets of data across the same categories
solve.work: Two bars per category compare two data sets across the same categories.

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: The temperatures at noon on four days were 61, 65, 58 and 70 degrees. What is the range of the temperatures?
questions.solution: Range = greatest - least = $70 - 58 = 12$ degrees.

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: How do you find the range of a set of numbers?
choices: Subtract the least number from the greatest number
Find the number that appears most often
Find the number in the middle when they are in order
questions.answer: Subtract the least number from the greatest number
questions.solution: The range is the difference between the greatest and least values.

solve.answer: Subtract the least number from the greatest number

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: The heights of 6 plants in centimeters are 14, 9, 22, 17, 12 and 20. What is the range of the heights, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Greatest 22, least 9. Range = $22 - 9 = 13$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Mode
questions.stem: A team scored 2, 0, 3, 2, 1, 2 and 3 goals in its seven games. What is the mode of the number of goals?
questions.solution: The number 2 appears three times, more than any other number (3 appears twice), so the mode is 2.

solve.work: Counts: 0 once, 1 once, 2 three times, 3 twice. Mode 2.

questions.skill: Mode
questions.stem: Which description matches the mode of a data set?
choices: The greatest value minus the least value
The value that occurs most often
The middle value when the data are in order
The total of all the values
questions.answer: The value that occurs most often
questions.solution: The mode is the value that appears the most times.

solve.answer: The value that occurs most often
solve.work: Mode is the value that occurs most often.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: Five boxes hold 6, 8, 9, 12 and 14 crayons. What is the median number of crayons?
questions.solution: The numbers are already in order. The middle one of the five is 9.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: Which description matches the median of a data set?
choices: The value that occurs most often
The greatest value minus the least value
The middle value when the data are listed in order
questions.answer: The middle value when the data are listed in order
questions.solution: The median is the middle value after the data are put in order from least to greatest.

solve.answer: The middle value when the data are listed in order
solve.work: Median is the middle value of ordered data.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from data
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the favorite pets of 28 students: dogs 14, cats 9, fish 5. Which conclusion is supported by the data?
choices: Every student in the school likes dogs best
Fish are the most popular pet
Cats are the least popular pet
More of these students chose dogs than any other pet
questions.answer: More of these students chose dogs than any other pet
questions.solution: Dogs have the tallest bar (14). Fish (5) are the least popular, and the data cannot speak for the whole school.

solve.answer: More of these students chose dogs than any other pet
solve.work: Dogs 14 is the most of these 28 students. Fish (5) is least, not cats; the data say nothing about every student in the school.

questions.skill: Median of a data set
questions.stem: Seven students read 12, 8, 15, 10, 9, 11 and 14 pages. What is the median number of pages?
questions.solution: Put the numbers in order: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15. The median is the middle number. With 7 numbers, the middle is the 4th, which is 11.

questions.skill: Total from a frequency table
questions.stem: Students were asked how many siblings they have. 0 siblings: 5 students. 1 sibling: 9 students. 2 siblings: 6 students. 3 siblings: 2 students. How many students were asked in all?
questions.solution: Add the number of students in every row: 5 + 9 + 6 + 2 = 22. (6 is 0 + 1 + 2 + 3, the number of siblings added up, not the number of students.)

questions.skill: Read a line plot described in words
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of goals a team scored in 10 games. There are 2 Xs above 0, 3 Xs above 1, 4 Xs above 2 and 1 X above 3. In how many games did the team score more than 1 goal?
questions.solution: Each X is one game. More than 1 goal means 2 goals or 3 goals. There are 4 Xs above 2 and 1 X above 3, so 4 + 1 = 5 games.

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Which pair shows a numerical question first and a categorical question second?
choices: What kind of book do you like? / How many pages are in your book?
How many pages are in your book? / How many books did you read?
What kind of book do you like? / Who is your favorite writer?
How many pages are in your book? / What kind of book do you like?
questions.answer: How many pages are in your book? / What kind of book do you like?
questions.solution: "How many pages" is answered with a number (numerical). "What kind of book" is answered with words (categorical). The pair must be in that order.

solve.answer: How many pages are in your book? / What kind of book do you like?
solve.work: Need numerical then categorical. 'How many pages...' is numerical; 'What kind of book...' is categorical. Option 2 matches. Option 1 is numerical/numerical, option 3 reversed, option 4 categorical/categorical.

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Six survey questions are listed. 1. How many minutes do you practice piano? 2. What instrument do you play? 3. How many students are in your music class? 4. Which song is your favorite? 5. How old were you when you began lessons? 6. Do you like to sing? How many of the six questions are numerical questions?
questions.solution: Questions 1, 3 and 5 are answered with numbers. Questions 2, 4 and 6 are answered with names or yes and no, so they are categorical. That makes 3 numerical questions.

solve.work: 1 minutes: numerical. 2 instrument: categorical. 3 how many students: numerical. 4 song: categorical. 5 age began: numerical. 6 yes/no: categorical. Numerical: 1, 3, 5 = 3.

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Maya wants to show her classmates' answers on a line plot, which needs numbers on a number line. Which question should she ask?
choices: What is your favorite bedtime story?
How many hours did you sleep last night?
Which room do you sleep in?
questions.answer: How many hours did you sleep last night?
questions.solution: A line plot shows numerical data. Only the question about hours has numbers as answers.

solve.answer: How many hours did you sleep last night?
solve.work: A line plot needs numerical answers. Only 'How many hours did you sleep last night?' gives numbers.

questions.skill: Plan how to collect data
questions.stem: A teacher wants to know how many minutes students at the school spend getting to school each day. Which plan will give the best data?
choices: Ask students from every grade how many minutes it takes them to get to school
Ask only the students who ride the bus
Ask students whether they like their trip to school
Ask only the students who arrive first in the morning
questions.answer: Ask students from every grade how many minutes it takes them to get to school
questions.solution: The plan must ask for a number of minutes and must include students from the whole school, not just one group.

solve.answer: Ask students from every grade how many minutes it takes them to get to school
solve.work: The question is about minutes for all students; asking students from every grade how many minutes gives numerical data from the whole school. Others are biased samples or ask the wrong question.

questions.skill: Plan how to collect data
questions.stem: Four steps for working with data are listed. (1) Draw a conclusion. (2) Collect the data. (3) Ask a question. (4) Make a graph of the data. Which list shows the steps in the best order?
questions.solution: First ask a question (3), then collect the data (2), then make a graph (4), and last draw a conclusion (1).

solve.work: Data cycle: ask a question (3), collect data (2), make a graph (4), draw a conclusion (1): 3, 2, 4, 1.

questions.skill: Choose a graph or a scale
questions.stem: The bars of a bar graph will show 20, 35, 40 and 15 students. The scale will count by the same number on each line. Which scale lets every bar end exactly on a line?
questions.solution: Every number must be a multiple of the scale. 20, 35, 40 and 15 are all multiples of 5. Counting by 10s misses 35 and 15, by 4s misses 35 and 15, and by 8s misses 20, 35 and 15.

solve.work: 20, 35, 40, 15 are all multiples of 5. By 10s fails for 35 and 15; by 8s fails for 20, 35, 15; by 4s fails for 35, 15. Count by 5s.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: Students were asked how many hours they watched TV last night. 0 hours: 3 students. 1 hour: 8 students. 2 hours: 7 students. 3 hours: 2 students. How many students watched TV for 2 hours or more?
questions.solution: 2 hours or more means 2 hours and 3 hours: $7 + 2 = 9$ students.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: The numbers of letters in the first names of 10 students are 4, 5, 5, 3, 6, 5, 4, 5, 6 and 3. In a frequency table of this data, what is the frequency of 5?
questions.solution: Count the 5s in the list: there are four of them, so the frequency of 5 is 4.

solve.work: Data 4,5,5,3,6,5,4,5,6,3: the 5s are the 2nd, 3rd, 6th and 8th values, so frequency 4.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: Students voted for a lunch. Pizza: 14. Tacos: 9. Pasta: 7. Salad: 4. How many students did NOT vote for pizza?
questions.solution: Add the other lunches: $9 + 7 + 4 = 20$ students.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: Students chose a favorite sport. Soccer: 14. Tennis: 9. Swimming: 14. Golf: 6. Which statement is true?
choices: Soccer and swimming got the same number of votes
Golf got more votes than tennis
Swimming got more votes than soccer
questions.answer: Soccer and swimming got the same number of votes
questions.solution: Soccer and swimming both got 14 votes, so they tie. Tennis (9) did not get the most, golf (6) got fewer than tennis, and swimming did not get more than soccer.

solve.answer: Soccer and swimming got the same number of votes
solve.work: Soccer 14 and swimming 14 are equal. Tennis 9 is not most; golf 6 < tennis 9; swimming not more than soccer.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of days 18 students were absent this month. There are 7 Xs above 0, 6 Xs above 1 and 3 Xs above 2. The rest of the Xs are above 3. How many Xs are above 3?
questions.solution: The first three stacks have $7 + 6 + 3 = 16$ Xs. The rest are $18 - 16 = 2$ Xs.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: Mina made a line plot of how many cookies each of 9 friends ate: 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6. Which statement describes her line plot?
questions.solution: The value 4 appears three times, so there are 3 Xs above 4. The value 3 appears twice, and 6 and 2 appear once each.

solve.work: Counts: 2 once, 3 twice, 4 three times, 5 twice, 6 once. Only '3 Xs above 4' is true.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of marbles in 10 bags. There are 2 Xs above 10, no Xs above 11, 5 Xs above 12 and 3 Xs above 13. How many of the bags have more than 11 marbles?
questions.solution: More than 11 means 12 or 13 marbles: $5 + 3 = 8$ bags.

questions.skill: Line plot with fractional measurements
questions.stem: Eight pieces of ribbon are measured to the nearest half inch. Their lengths in inches are 1, $1\frac{1}{2}$, $1\frac{1}{2}$, 2, 2, 2, $2\frac{1}{2}$ and 3. What is the range of the lengths, in inches?
questions.solution: The longest is 3 inches and the shortest is 1 inch. Range = $3 - 1 = 2$ inches.

questions.skill: Line plot with fractional measurements
questions.stem: A line plot shows the lengths of bean sprouts. There are 3 Xs above $\frac{1}{2}$ inch, 5 Xs above 1 inch and 4 Xs above $1\frac{1}{2}$ inches. How many sprouts are 1 inch long or longer?
questions.solution: Sprouts of 1 inch or more are the ones at 1 inch and at $1\frac{1}{2}$ inches: $5 + 4 = 9$.

questions.skill: Read a bar graph
questions.stem: The scale of a bar graph counts by 5s. The bar for Monday reaches 35. The bar for Tuesday is 3 lines shorter than the bar for Monday. What number does Tuesday's bar show?
questions.solution: Each line is worth 5, so 3 lines is 15. Tuesday: $35 - 15 = 20$.

questions.skill: Read a bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the number of books checked out each day. Monday: 18. Tuesday: 24. Wednesday: 12. Thursday: 24. Friday: 20. Which two days had the same number of books checked out?
questions.solution: Tuesday and Thursday both reached 24.

solve.work: Tuesday 24 and Thursday 24 are equal; no other pair matches.

questions.skill: Read a bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the number of students in each club. Chess: 14. Art: 22. Drama: 18. Robotics: 10. How many more students must join Robotics for it to have as many students as Art?
questions.solution: $22 - 10 = 12$ more students.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph compares the pets in two classes. Dogs: Class 1 has 7 and Class 2 has 9. Cats: Class 1 has 6 and Class 2 has 4. Fish: Class 1 has 3 and Class 2 has 5. How many pets does Class 2 have in all?
questions.solution: Add Class 2's bars: $9 + 4 + 5 = 18$ pets.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph shows the rainfall in inches in two towns. January: Town A 4, Town B 6. February: Town A 5, Town B 5. March: Town A 8, Town B 6. April: Town A 7, Town B 9. In which month did Town A get more rain than Town B?
questions.solution: In March, Town A (8) is greater than Town B (6). In January and April Town B is greater, and in February they are equal.

solve.work: Jan 4<6, Feb 5=5, Mar 8>6, Apr 7<9. Only March.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: In a double bar graph the scale counts by 5s. A blue bar ends at 35. The red bar for the same category is 2 lines shorter. What number does the red bar show?
questions.solution: Two lines is $2 \times 5 = 10$. The red bar shows $35 - 10 = 25$.

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of pets owned by 12 students. There are Xs above 0, 1, 2 and 6, and no Xs above 3, 4 or 5. What is the range of the data?
questions.solution: The least value is 0 and the greatest is 6. Range = $6 - 0 = 6$.

questions.skill: Range, mode and median together
questions.stem: For the data 3, 7, 7, 9 and 14, which of these has the greatest value?
choices: The mode, the median and the range are all equal
questions.solution: Range = $14 - 3 = 11$. The mode is 7 (it appears twice). The median is the middle value, 7. So the range, 11, is the greatest.

solve.work: Mode 7, median 7, range 14 - 3 = 11. Range is greatest.

questions.skill: Mode
questions.stem: Students were asked how many siblings they have. 0 siblings: 4 students. 1 sibling: 9 students. 2 siblings: 7 students. 3 siblings: 2 students. What is the mode of the number of siblings?
questions.solution: The greatest frequency is 9, for 1 sibling, so the mode is 1.

questions.skill: Mode
questions.stem: Which data set has a mode of 8?
questions.solution: In 5, 8, 8, 9, 12 the number 8 appears twice and the others once. The second set has no repeats, the third repeats 5 and 9, and the fourth has a mode of 9.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: Five runners finished a race in 31, 27, 35, 29 and 33 seconds. What is the median time, in seconds?
questions.solution: In order: 27, 29, 31, 33, 35. The middle value is 31 seconds.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: Seven plants have heights of 18, 25, 21, 30, 16, 27 and 22 centimeters. What is the median height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: In order: 16, 18, 21, 22, 25, 27, 30. The middle (fourth) value is 22 centimeters.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: What is the median of 14, 6, 11, 9 and 3?
questions.solution: Put the numbers in order first: 3, 6, 9, 11, 14. The middle number is 9. (11 is only the middle of the list as written.)

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from data
questions.stem: A teacher counted the lunches students chose: pizza 11, salad 4, sandwich 7, soup 3. The cafeteria wants to make lunches that students will choose. Which choice is best supported by the data?
choices: Make more pizza than any other lunch
Make more soup than any other lunch
Make the same amount of every lunch
Stop making sandwiches because salad is more popular
questions.answer: Make more pizza than any other lunch
questions.solution: Pizza had the most votes (11). Soup had the fewest, and sandwich (7) was chosen more than salad (4).

solve.answer: Make more pizza than any other lunch
solve.work: Pizza 11 is the most chosen, so make more pizza. Soup is least; salad (4) is less popular than sandwiches (7).

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from data
questions.stem: Class A's test scores have a range of 8. Class B's test scores have a range of 25. Which conclusion is correct?
choices: Class A's scores are more spread out than Class B's
Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
Class B had the higher median score
Class A and Class B have the same spread
questions.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
questions.solution: The range shows how spread out the data are. A range of 25 is greater than 8, so Class B's scores are more spread out. The ranges say nothing about which class has the higher median.

solve.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
solve.work: Larger range means more spread: 25 > 8, so Class B is more spread out. Range says nothing about the median.

questions.skill: Median from a frequency table
questions.stem: Nine worms were measured to the nearest centimeter. 3 cm: 2 worms. 4 cm: 3 worms. 5 cm: 1 worm. 6 cm: 3 worms. What is the median length, in centimeters?
questions.solution: List the lengths in order: 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6. There are 9 lengths, so the median is the 5th one, which is 4 centimeters.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from two sets of data
questions.stem: Two classes voted for their favorite fruit. Class A: apples 8, bananas 6, grapes 4. Class B: apples 5, bananas 9, grapes 7. Which fruit got the most votes from the two classes together?
choices: They all got the same number
questions.solution: Add the two classes. Apples: 8 + 5 = 13. Bananas: 6 + 9 = 15. Grapes: 4 + 7 = 11. Bananas got the most votes. (Apples got the most votes in Class A alone.)

questions.skill: Range and mode together
questions.stem: Nine students' scores on a quiz are 5, 8, 6, 8, 7, 8, 5, 6 and 9. What is the sum of the range and the mode?
questions.solution: The range is 9 - 5 = 4. The mode is the most common score: 8 appears 3 times, 5 and 6 appear twice, 7 and 9 once. So the mode is 8. The sum is 4 + 8 = 12.

questions.skill: Numerical or categorical question
questions.stem: Leo asked, "How do you get to school?" The answers were walk, bus, car, bus, bike, walk, car, bus. Which statement is true?
choices: It is a numerical question, and the mode is bus
It is a categorical question, and the mode is walk
It is a categorical question, and the mode is bus
It is a numerical question, and the mode is car
questions.answer: It is a categorical question, and the mode is bus
questions.solution: The answers are words, so the question is categorical. Bus appears 3 times, walk 2, car 2 and bike 1, so the mode is bus.

solve.answer: It is a categorical question, and the mode is bus
solve.work: Answers are words, so categorical. Counts: walk 2, bus 3, car 2, bike 1. Mode is bus.

questions.skill: Choose a graph or a scale
questions.stem: The scale of a bar graph counts by 4s: 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. One bar ends exactly halfway between the lines for 20 and 24. What number does the bar show?
questions.solution: Halfway between 20 and 24 is $(20 + 24) \div 2 = 22$.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: A class of 30 students was asked how many pets each has. 0 pets: 6 students. 1 pet: 11 students. 2 pets: 7 students. 4 pets: 2 students. The rest of the students have 3 pets. How many students have 3 pets?
questions.solution: The rows given total $6 + 11 + 7 + 2 = 26$ students. The rest are $30 - 26 = 4$ students.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: A frequency table shows how many siblings students have. 0 siblings: 6 students. 1 sibling: 10 students. 2 siblings: 9 students. 3 siblings: 5 students. Which statement is true?
choices: The most common number of siblings is 3
More students have 1 sibling than any other number of siblings
Exactly 15 students have 2 or more siblings
questions.answer: More students have 1 sibling than any other number of siblings
questions.solution: 10 students have 1 sibling, which is the greatest count. 2 or more siblings is $9 + 5 = 14$ students, and the total asked is $6 + 10 + 9 + 5 = 30$ students.

solve.answer: More students have 1 sibling than any other number of siblings
solve.work: Total 6+10+9+5 = 30. Most common is 1 (10), not 3. Not 24 asked. 2 or more: 9+5 = 14, not 15. 1 sibling (10) is more than any other: true.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: A team's goals per game are in a frequency table. 0 goals: 2 games. 1 goal: 4 games. 2 goals: 3 games. 3 goals: 1 game. How many goals did the team score in all?
questions.solution: Multiply each number of goals by its number of games and add: $0 \times 2 + 1 \times 4 + 2 \times 3 + 3 \times 1 = 0 + 4 + 6 + 3 = 13$ goals.

questions.skill: Frequency tables and tally marks
questions.stem: The numbers of cavities found in 15 children are 0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 1, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0, 4, 1, 2 and 0. How many of the children had at least 2 cavities?
questions.solution: The values that are 2 or more are 2, 3, 2, 4 and 2. That is 5 children.

solve.work: Tally: 0 five times, 1 five times, 2 three times, 3 once, 4 once (total 15). At least 2: 3 + 1 + 1 = 5.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: Students voted for a class pet. The turtle got 6 votes. The hamster got 3 more votes than the turtle. The fish got twice as many votes as the turtle. How many votes did the hamster and the fish get altogether?
questions.solution: Hamster: $6 + 3 = 9$ votes. Fish: $2 \times 6 = 12$ votes. Together: $9 + 12 = 21$ votes.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: In a survey, 12 students chose tennis and 9 students chose volleyball. Basketball got 7 more votes than tennis. How many students chose tennis, volleyball or basketball?
questions.solution: Basketball: $12 + 7 = 19$ votes. All three: $12 + 9 + 19 = 40$ students.

questions.skill: Compare categories in a table
questions.stem: Students voted for a pet. Dog: 15. Cat: 12. Bird: 3. Fish: 6. Which statement is true?
choices: Cats got twice as many votes as dogs
Birds and fish together got as many votes as cats
Dogs and cats together got more than twice as many votes as birds and fish together
Dogs got 5 more votes than cats
questions.answer: Dogs and cats together got more than twice as many votes as birds and fish together
questions.solution: Dogs and cats: $15 + 12 = 27$. Birds and fish: $3 + 6 = 9$, and twice 9 is 18, which is less than 27. Cats did not get twice the dogs, 9 is not 12, and dogs got 3 more than cats, not 5.

solve.answer: Dogs and cats together got more than twice as many votes as birds and fish together
solve.work: Dogs+cats = 27; birds+fish = 9; twice 9 = 18; 27 > 18 true. Birds+fish 9 vs cats 12 false. Dogs - cats = 3, not 5. Cats are not twice dogs.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the hours students slept. There are 2 Xs above 6, 4 Xs above 7, 7 Xs above 8, 3 Xs above 9 and 1 X above 10. Which statement is true?
choices: The same number of students slept 7 hours and 9 hours
More students slept 8 hours than any other number of hours
questions.answer: More students slept 8 hours than any other number of hours
questions.solution: The stack above 8 is the tallest (7). Hours 7 and 9 have 4 and 3 Xs. The total is $2 + 4 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 17$ students, and 2 students slept 6 hours.

solve.answer: More students slept 8 hours than any other number of hours
solve.work: Counts 2, 4, 7, 3, 1 (total 17). 6 hours had 2, not 1. 17 is not fewer than 15. 8 hours (7) is the most: true. 7 hours 4 vs 9 hours 3: not equal.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of apples picked by 12 children. There is 1 X above 2, 2 Xs above 3, 4 Xs above 4, 3 Xs above 5 and 2 Xs above 6. How many apples were picked altogether?
questions.solution: Multiply each number of apples by its number of Xs and add: $2 + 6 + 16 + 15 + 12 = 51$ apples.

questions.skill: Read or build a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot of 20 quiz scores has Xs above 6, 7, 8 and 9 only. There are 3 Xs above 6. There are twice as many Xs above 7 as above 6. There are 5 Xs above 8. The rest are above 9. How many Xs are above 9?
questions.solution: Above 7 there are $2 \times 3 = 6$ Xs. Above 6, 7 and 8 there are $3 + 6 + 5 = 14$ Xs. The rest are $20 - 14 = 6$ Xs above 9.

solve.work: Above 6: 3. Above 7: 2 x 3 = 6. Above 8: 5. Sum 14. Above 9: 20 - 14 = 6.

questions.skill: Line plot with fractional measurements
questions.stem: A line plot shows the lengths of carrots in inches. The shortest carrot is $2\frac{1}{4}$ inches and the longest is $4\frac{3}{4}$ inches. What is the range of the lengths, in inches?
questions.solution: Range = $4\frac{3}{4} - 2\frac{1}{4} = 2\frac{2}{4} = 2\frac{1}{2}$ inches.

questions.skill: Line plot with fractional measurements
questions.stem: Seven pieces of string measure $3\frac{1}{2}$, $2\frac{1}{4}$, $3\frac{1}{4}$, $2\frac{3}{4}$, $3\frac{1}{2}$, $2\frac{1}{2}$ and 3 inches. What is the median length, in inches?
questions.solution: In order: $2\frac{1}{4}$, $2\frac{1}{2}$, $2\frac{3}{4}$, 3, $3\frac{1}{4}$, $3\frac{1}{2}$, $3\frac{1}{2}$. The middle (fourth) value is 3 inches.

solve.work: In order: 2 1/4, 2 1/2, 2 3/4, 3, 3 1/4, 3 1/2, 3 1/2. Seven values, middle (4th) is 3.

questions.skill: Read a bar graph
questions.stem: The bars of a bar graph show 36, 28, 44 and 32 pages read by four students. The scale counts by 4s. How many lines taller is the tallest bar than the shortest bar?
questions.solution: The tallest bar is 44 and the shortest is 28, a difference of 16. Each line is 4, so that is $16 \div 4 = 4$ lines.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph compares the books three students read in May and in June. Ali: May 8, June 12. Bea: May 10, June 7. Cam: May 6, June 9. How many more books did the three students read in June than in May?
questions.solution: June: $12 + 7 + 9 = 28$. May: $8 + 10 + 6 = 24$. The difference is $28 - 24 = 4$ books.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph shows how many girls and how many boys joined four clubs. Girls: art 9, chess 12, drama 7, music 10. Boys: art 11, chess 8, drama 7, music 13. How many more boys than girls joined the four clubs in all?

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph shows the books read by two grades. Fall: Grade 3 read 12 and Grade 4 read 15. Spring: Grade 3 read 18 and Grade 4 read 15. Which statement is true?
choices: Grade 3 read fewer books in the spring than in the fall
Grade 4 read the same number of books in the fall and in the spring
Grade 4 read more books than Grade 3 in the spring
Grade 3 and Grade 4 read the same number of books in the fall
questions.answer: Grade 4 read the same number of books in the fall and in the spring
questions.solution: Grade 4 read 15 in both seasons. Grade 3 went up from 12 to 18, in the spring Grade 3 (18) beat Grade 4 (15), and in the fall they read 12 and 15.

solve.answer: Grade 4 read the same number of books in the fall and in the spring
solve.work: Spring: G4 15 < G3 18, so A false. G3 spring 18 > fall 12, B false. Fall 12 vs 15, C false. G4 15 fall and 15 spring: D true.

questions.skill: Double bar graph: compare two data sets
questions.stem: A double bar graph compares sales of lemonade and cookies on three days. Lemonade: Friday 14, Saturday 22, Sunday 18. Cookies: Friday 9, Saturday 26, Sunday 15. What is the greatest difference between the two bars on any one day?
questions.solution: Differences: Friday $14 - 9 = 5$, Saturday $26 - 22 = 4$, Sunday $18 - 15 = 3$. The greatest is 5.

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: The scores on a quiz have a range of 15. The lowest score is 78. What is the highest score?
questions.solution: Range = highest - lowest, so highest = lowest + range = $78 + 15 = 93$.

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: Set A is 12, 18, 25 and 30. Set B is 5, 20, 22 and 40. How much greater is the range of Set B than the range of Set A?
questions.solution: Range of A: $30 - 12 = 18$. Range of B: $40 - 5 = 35$. The difference is $35 - 18 = 17$.

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: The numbers 8, 12, 15 and 11 have a range of 7. Jada adds one more number that is greater than all four, and the range becomes 12. What number did she add?
questions.solution: The least number is still 8, so the new greatest number is $8 + 12 = 20$. It is greater than 15, as the question says.

solve.work: Least stays 8; new greatest x with x - 8 = 12, so x = 20 (greater than 15, consistent).

questions.skill: Mode
questions.stem: The list 4, 7, 4, 9, 7, 4, 7 has two modes. What number could be added to the list so that the new list has just one mode, and that mode is 7?
questions.solution: Right now 4 and 7 each appear three times. Adding another 7 makes four 7s, so 7 is the only mode. Adding any other number would leave a tie or make a different number the mode.

solve.work: 4 appears 3 times, 7 appears 3 times, 9 once. Adding 7 makes 7 appear 4 times, the only mode. Adding 4 gives mode 4; adding anything else leaves two modes. So 7 is the only answer.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of pets owned by 11 students. There are 3 Xs above 0, 4 Xs above 1, 2 Xs above 2 and 2 Xs above 3. What is the median number of pets?
questions.solution: With 11 values, the median is the 6th value in order. The first 3 values are 0, the next 4 are 1 (values 4 to 7), so the 6th value is 1.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: Eight children have shoe sizes 6, 4, 5, 3, 5, 7, 4 and 5. What is the median shoe size?
questions.solution: In order: 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7. The two middle values (fourth and fifth) are both 5, so the median is 5.

solve.work: Order: 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7. Eight values; 4th and 5th are both 5, so the median is 5.

questions.skill: Median
questions.stem: The median of five numbers is 12. Four of the numbers are 5, 9, 15 and 20. What is the fifth number?
questions.solution: The median is the middle number when the five are in order. With 5, 9, 15 and 20, the fifth number must sit between 9 and 15 to be the middle, so it is the median itself: 12.

solve.work: With 5, 9, 15, 20 and x: if x <= 9 the median is 9; if x >= 15 it is 15; if 9 < x < 15 the median is x. Median 12 forces x = 12.

questions.skill: Range, mode and median together
questions.stem: For the data 4, 6, 6, 7, 9, 12 and 6, which statement is true?
choices: The mode is 6 and the median is 7
The mode and the median are both 6
questions.answer: The mode and the median are both 6
questions.solution: In order: 4, 6, 6, 6, 7, 9, 12. The mode is 6 (three times) and the middle value is 6. The range is $12 - 4 = 8$.

solve.answer: The mode and the median are both 6
solve.work: Order: 4, 6, 6, 6, 7, 9, 12. Mode 6, median (4th) 6, range 8. Only 'both 6' is true.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from data
questions.stem: A line plot shows the hours students read last night. 0 hours: 2 Xs. 1 hour: 6 Xs. 2 hours: 9 Xs. 3 hours: 5 Xs. 4 hours: 2 Xs. How many more students read 2 hours or more than read fewer than 2 hours?
questions.solution: 2 hours or more: $9 + 5 + 2 = 16$ students. Fewer than 2 hours: $2 + 6 = 8$ students. The difference is $16 - 8 = 8$.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from data
questions.stem: Mia asked 10 students in the lunch line which subject they like best. Seven said math, so she says, "Most students in my school like math best." Why might her conclusion be wrong?
choices: Seven is not more than half of ten
Math cannot be a favorite subject
A conclusion can only be drawn from a line plot
She asked only a few students in one place, so they may not stand for the whole school
questions.answer: She asked only a few students in one place, so they may not stand for the whole school
questions.solution: Seven out of ten is more than half, but only 10 students in one spot were asked. They may not match the whole school, so the conclusion is not well supported.

solve.answer: She asked only a few students in one place, so they may not stand for the whole school
solve.work: 10 students in one lunch line may not represent the whole school. Seven is more than half of ten, so option 3 is false.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from data
questions.stem: Two classes made line plots of the books each student read. Class 1 read 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5 and 6 books. Class 2 read 1, 3, 5, 5, 5, 7 and 9 books. Which statement is true?
choices: Both classes have the same mode and median, but Class 2 has the greater range
questions.answer: Both classes have the same mode and median, but Class 2 has the greater range
questions.solution: Both lists have mode 5 and median 5. The range of Class 1 is $6 - 3 = 3$ and of Class 2 is $9 - 1 = 8$, so Class 2 has the greater range.

solve.answer: Both classes have the same mode and median, but Class 2 has the greater range
solve.work: Class 1: mode 5, median 5, range 3. Class 2: mode 5, median 5, range 8. So same mode and median, Class 2 greater range.
